reviews.dimension: Compliance with the official Case Study 1 requirements (ground rules, Round 1 / Round 2 deliverables, rubric)
reviews.summary: I read the Case Study 1 PDF (4 pages: layers, ground rules, dataset, round deliverables, rubric), docs/OFFICIAL_REQUIREMENTS.md R1-R15, the Round 1 slide content and rendered PNG, the Round 2 deck plan, CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX, SYSTEM_DESIGN, DEMO_RUNBOOK/SCRIPT, KNOWN_LIMITATIONS, the code behind each row (cli, pipeline, agent, retrain, clean, dashboard, e4 script, configs), and opened every metrics.json, e0/e3/e4/e6 summary.json, retrain_log.json, mlflow.db and sentinelloop.db (read-only); I ran the fast test suite (97 passed, 103 collected). No ground rule is violated (no LLM anywhere in the lock file or source, open-source stack, one-command pipeline, all four C-MAPSS subsets) and all four PDF-named Round 1 items are visibly on the slide; the worst problems are that the "retraining flow when new data arrives" is not wired anywhere in the package (R7 is marked VERIFIED, SYSTEM_DESIGN documents a trigger, CLI commands and DB tables that do not exist), the scripted FD001 demo cannot show the PROMOTE path because every FD001 gate decision in the stored log is REJECT, the anomaly-detection half of the ML layer has no reported performance on real degradation and never creates a work order, and the slide to be uploaded still carries a team/college placeholder. Overall verdict: compliant in substance, but three status/document claims overstate what is built and must be corrected before a judge or compliance reviewer compares the documents with the artefacts.

findings.title: R7 'retraining flow when new data arrives' marked VERIFIED, but no trigger exists in the package
findings.issue: R7 status reads 'VERIFIED: ... drift/new-data trigger + gated promotion'. The PDF's MLOps layer asks to 'show a simple retraining flow when new data arrives'. Nothing in src/sentinelloop watches for new data or starts a retrain on a drift alarm; the only retraining lives in an experiment script that runs its scenarios unconditionally.
findings.evidence: src/sentinelloop/retrain.py is 35 lines containing only evaluate_gate(); grep -rniE 'new data|trigger|retrain' src/sentinelloop/*.py returns no trigger code (only policy.trigger_series and dashboard reads). experiments/e4_retrain_gate.py lines 92-106 call scenario('A_accept_more_data') and scenario('B_reject_corrupted_data') unconditionally; the drift check (lines 108-135) is computed afterwards and gates nothing. pipeline.py line 180 uses drift_report.alarm only as an agent escalation input. The slide box 'RETRAIN JOB triggered by a drift alarm or a new data file' (make_round1_slide.py:85) therefore describes design intent, not code.
findings.recommendation: Either add a minimal `python -m sentinelloop retrain --subset X` that runs when a file appears under data/incoming/ or when the stored drift report has alarm=true, and log it, or downgrade R7 to PARTIALLY VERIFIED ('gate and promotion verified; trigger is a scripted experiment') and reword the slide box to 'retrain job (gated); trigger: drift alarm or new file (design)'.

findings.title: SYSTEM_DESIGN.md documents CLI commands, a retrain trigger, DB tables and artefacts that do not exist, while PROJECT_STATUS says it is aligned
findings.issue: The PDF ground rule is 'document the design clearly so it can be explained in a review'. The final design doc lists `cli.py` commands 'doctor, data, train, evaluate, replay, stress, retrain, stream, dashboard, run' (line 65), a retrain.py 'Trigger (new data file in data/incoming/ or drift alarm)' (line 61), SQLite tables 'retrain_log, drift_log' (line 70) and artefacts 'model_quantile.pkl', 'predictions_oof_train.csv' (line 68). PROJECT_STATUS.md line 54 states 'docs/SYSTEM_DESIGN.md ... aligned with the built components'.
findings.evidence: src/sentinelloop/cli.py lines 85-92 register only doctor, data, baseline, run, audit, dashboard. Read-only sqlite query of artifacts/sentinelloop.db: tables = ['decisions', 'work_orders', 'runs']. ls artifacts/FD001 shows model_cqr.pkl and no predictions_oof_train.csv. No data/incoming handling anywhere in src/.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite rows 61, 65, 68, 70 of SYSTEM_DESIGN.md to the built interface (six CLI commands, three tables, model_cqr.pkl, OOF predictions under experiments/results/oof) and remove the 'aligned' claim from PROJECT_STATUS until a doc-vs-code check has been run.

findings.title: Scripted demo retraining run is on FD001, whose stored retrain log contains only REJECT decisions (no PROMOTE row to show)
findings.issue: Round 2 requires 'a demo retraining run'. The runbook produces artefacts with `run --subset FD001` (line 16) and tells the presenter to show 'retraining log with the PROMOTE and REJECT rows' (line 36). On FD001 the expected-PROMOTE scenario was rejected in both E4 runs, so the dashboard will show rows with as_expected:false and no accept path. The Round 1 slide also states 'accept AND reject paths are demonstrated' (make_round1_slide.py:92) without saying on which subsets.
findings.evidence: artifacts/FD001/retrain_log.json: decisions = A_accept_more_data REJECT ('picp 0.800 < 0.85'), B REJECT, secondary A REJECT ('picp 0.835 < 0.85'), B REJECT, B2 REJECT. experiments/results/e4_retrain_gate/summary.json and e4_retrain_gate_secondary/summary.json: PROMOTE on A occurs only for FD002 and FD003 (both runs) and FD004 (primary only). Python listing of all four retrain logs confirms FD001 has zero PROMOTE rows.
findings.recommendation: Run the demo on FD003 (PROMOTE and REJECT with reasons in both runs, 100 test engines, RMSE 13.88) or show the FD003 log explicitly; add the subset name next to 'accept AND reject paths are demonstrated' on the slide and in the deck.

findings.title: Rendered Round 1 slide still carries a team/college placeholder
findings.issue: The file that would be uploaded reads 'Team SentinelLoop · (college to be filled)' in the title band. The Unstop listing (quoted in OFFICIAL_REQUIREMENTS.md line 15) requires 2-3 members from the same college; a slide with a placeholder reads as unfinished and may fail an identity check.
findings.evidence: round1_slide.png top-right text: 'Team SentinelLoop · (college to be filled)'. make_round1_slide.py line 51 default `--team 'Team ______  ·  ______ College'`. OFFICIAL_REQUIREMENTS.md line 63 R14: 'PARTIALLY VERIFIED: ... team/college placeholder'.
findings.recommendation: Re-render with `--team` set to the real names before upload and make the script refuse to write the PDF when the team string contains '___' or 'to be filled'.

findings.title: FD004 raw RMSE quoted as 27.1 in two submission documents; the artefact and the rendered slide say 27.0
findings.issue: C1 and round1_slide_content.md line 37 state 'FD004 15.4 / 27.1'. The artefact value is 27.0486, which the slide script prints as 27.0. The matrix's own promise is that every number is copied from an artefact, so the two documents disagree with the artefact and with the slide a judge will see.
findings.evidence: artifacts/FD004/metrics.json hgbr_rmse_raw = 27.048590629322145; experiments/results/e0_baseline/FD004_metrics.json identical. round1_slide.png bottom-left: 'FD004 15.4 / 27.0'. CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md line 7: 'FD004 15.4/27.1'. round1_slide_content.md line 37: 'FD004 15.4 / 27.1'. README.md line 14 and round2_deck_content.md line 11 correctly say 27.05.
findings.recommendation: Change both documents to 27.0 (or print two decimals everywhere) and add a one-line script that diffs every number in the matrix against the JSON it cites.

findings.title: Anomaly detection (half of the PDF's ML layer) has no reported performance on real degradation and never produces a work order
findings.issue: R4 'Detect abnormal behaviour' is marked VERIFIED on the strength of a unit test and a WATCH rule. No metric is reported for detection of actual degradation (lead time before failure, false-positive rate in healthy life on out-of-fold engines); the only anomaly numbers in the artefacts are flag rates without ground truth. The entry's own results document admits the anomaly input changes nothing in the policy metrics, and the agent code shows WATCH can never open an order.
findings.evidence: artifacts/<subset>/metrics.json contains only anomaly_flag_rate_test_last_cycle (0.16 / 0.19 / 0.22 / 0.08) and anomaly_threshold. tests/test_anomaly.py lines 15-24 assert only that late-life flags exceed early-life flags and early-life rate <= 0.10. docs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md line 93: 'ablation (iii) "anomaly input to the agent" was not run; by construction the anomaly input only sets WATCH severities and the conflicting-evidence escalation reason, neither of which enters the E1 policy metrics'. src/sentinelloop/agent.py line 88-89 (WATCH only when lower > t_medium) and line 15 ORDER_SEVERITIES = ('HIGH', 'CRITICAL'). E3 measures injected faults, not degradation.
findings.recommendation: Add an out-of-fold evaluation on complete training engines: cycles between first sustained flag and failure (lead time), fraction of engines flagged before failure, false-alarm rate in the first 40% of life; report it in metrics.json and on deck slide 5, and state plainly that the health index informs WATCH/escalation only.

findings.title: '33-46 s per subset' is quoted as the pipeline runtime but the stored metrics.json files record 51-76 s
findings.issue: C18, OFFICIAL_REQUIREMENTS R11 (line 60), REPRODUCIBILITY.md line 56 ('metrics elapsed_s') and deck slide 3 all say 33-46 s. The artefacts currently on disk were regenerated after the cited log and record longer times; the cited evidence ('elapsed_s in metrics') contradicts the claim.
findings.evidence: artifacts/FD001..FD004/metrics.json elapsed_s = 51.0, 61.9, 53.0, 76.0 (mtimes 03:28-03:31). experiments/results/full_run_stage1_pipeline.log lines 18/26/34/42 'done in 33.2 / 46.4 / 34.6 / 39.4 s' (mtime 03:23, earlier run).
findings.recommendation: Quote the range from the artefacts a judge will open ('about 1 minute per subset, 51-76 s in metrics.json') or regenerate and re-cite consistently.

findings.title: Round 1 slide has no problem-understanding block although it is 15% of the Round 1 rubric
findings.issue: The PDF scores 'Problem understanding (15%): clear and accurate grasp of the problem and its objectives'. The slide's title band states the solution thesis only; nothing restates the operational problem (unplanned downtime, fixed service intervals, human only for exceptions) or the objectives. SCORING_AND_RISKS.md line 7 self-scores 8.3/10 on 'Closed-loop framing in the PDF's words', which the rendered slide does not contain.
findings.evidence: round1_slide.png title band: 'Closed-loop prognostics that raise work orders from the RUL uncertainty LOWER bound, escalate only untrustworthy cases to a human, retrain only through a promotion gate, and make every decision auditable.' No panel or line mentions downtime, fixed intervals, breakdowns or the objective of the closed loop; make_round1_slide.py lines 62-64 are the only title-band text.
findings.recommendation: Add two lines under the title: the problem in the PDF's words (failures caught after breakdown or by fixed intervals; cost of unplanned downtime) and the objective (detect early, predict RUL, raise orders automatically, human only for exceptions).

findings.title: Slide body text is 6.3-6.7 pt on a 13.3 in canvas; the content plan claims 'readable at thumbnail scale'
findings.issue: Communication quality (5%) and every other criterion depend on the judge being able to read the slide. Roughly 70 lines of 6.3-6.7 pt text are packed into three panels plus a two-row diagram; at PDF-viewer fit-to-page on a laptop this is near the legibility floor, and the design rule in round1_slide_content.md line 5 ('Readable at thumbnail scale') is not met.
findings.evidence: make_round1_slide.py: bullets() default fs=6.5 (line 44), architecture boxes fs=6.7 (line 80), loop boxes fs=6.4 (line 87), agent table fs=6.4 (lines 134-149), footer fs=6.3 (lines 189-190). Rendered PNG at 2000 px width shows the three panels filled edge to edge.
findings.recommendation: Cut body text by about 40% (move the leakage-audit numbers, PHM08 convention and Round 2 preview to the deck), raise the minimum font to 8 pt, and check the PDF at 100% on a 1366 px laptop.

findings.title: 'Cluster purity 100%' claimed for FD002 and FD004; evidence exists only for FD004
findings.issue: The slide ('k = 6 for FD002/FD004, cluster purity 100%'), round1_slide_content.md line 15, deck slide 4 and matrix row C6 all attribute 100% purity to both multi-regime subsets. The cited evidence records a purity measurement only for FD004.
findings.evidence: docs/DECISION_LOG.md line 19 D14: 'Cluster purity 100% on FD004'. docs/REPRODUCIBILITY.md line 16: 'cluster purity on FD004 = 100%'. grep 'purity' over experiments/results finds no stored measurement for FD002; no purity key exists in any summary.json or metrics.json.
findings.recommendation: Compute and store purity for FD002 (one line against the six known operating conditions) or restrict the claim to FD004.

findings.title: 'Tests written before the code' is asserted on the slide and marked VERIFIED, but there is no version history to support it
findings.issue: The footer says 'pytest (tests written before the code)', deck slide 3 says '103 tests written before the code', and CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX C19 marks the TDD claim VERIFIED. The cited evidence only shows that the tests pass; the workspace is not a git repository, so ordering cannot be demonstrated to a judge.
findings.evidence: Environment reports 'Is a git repository: false'. CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md line 25 evidence = 'tests/, experiments/results/test_full_phase5.log' (log tail: exit=0, 103 passed). My run: `pytest tests -q -m 'not slow'` 97 passed; `--collect-only` sums to 103.
findings.recommendation: Keep '103 tests, all passing' and drop 'written before the code' from judged material, or initialise a repository so the history can back the process claim.

findings.title: PDF asks the cleaning step to handle 'basic noise'; no denoising or outlier treatment is active in cleaning
findings.issue: The Data Engineering layer requires 'clean it - handle missing values and basic noise'. The cleaner imputes missing values and normalises per regime; the only denoising function (EMA) is disabled by config, and no clipping/winsorising or outlier flagging exists in the cleaning path. Noise handling is delegated to the rolling-mean feature, which the slide states, but a judge reading the Data engineering criterion may score the cleaning layer as incomplete.
findings.evidence: configs/default.yaml line 8 `ema_alpha: 0.0 # causal EMA denoising DISABLED by default`. clean.py: impute() (lines 18-31) and CleanState (44-107) contain no outlier handling. docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md line 15: '"basic noise handling" is therefore the per-unit imputation plus the rolling-window features'.
findings.recommendation: Add a cheap, train-fitted, test-backed step (for example per-regime clipping at the 0.1/99.9 training percentiles with a flag that feeds the agent's quality input) and ablate it in E7, or state on the slide in one clause that noise is absorbed by the 20-cycle rolling mean and why EMA was rejected.

findings.title: Slide footer says Python 3.11 while the stored baseline run records Python 3.12.1
findings.issue: Footer text 'Tools: Python 3.11 · pandas · scikit-learn ...' does not match the interpreter version stored with the numbers printed on the same slide.
findings.evidence: experiments/results/e0_baseline/FD001_metrics.json 'versions': {'python': '3.12.1', 'sklearn': '1.7.2', ...}. pyproject.toml requires-python '>=3.11'.
findings.recommendation: Print 'Python 3.11+' or read the version from the metrics file like the other numbers.

findings.title: Health index described as top-3 deviations in two documents; configuration and artefact use top-2
findings.issue: round1_slide_content.md ('top-3 sensor deviations') and DECISION_LOG D10 ('RMS of the top-3 standardised deviations') disagree with the shipped configuration; the rendered slide hedges with 'top-k'.
findings.evidence: configs/default.yaml line 30 `top_k: 2`; artifacts/FD001/anomaly.json 'top_k': 2; docs/DECISION_LOG.md line 16 'top-3'.
findings.recommendation: Update D10 and the content plan to top-2 (and the reason for the change).

findings.title: round1_slide_content.md is stale relative to the rendered slide (deep challenger in MLflow, width > 60, baselines 'logged')
findings.issue: The content plan still says 'A deep challenger is logged in MLflow for comparison' (line 23) and 'interval width > 60' (line 33); PROJECT_STATUS line 60 says two unverifiable claims were removed from the script, but the plan was not updated. The rendered replacement 'RF and naive baselines are logged' can be read as MLflow logging, which does not happen.
findings.evidence: grep -i mlflow src/sentinelloop/baseline.py returns nothing; MLflow experiments (read-only query) are 'sentinelloop' (12 runs) and 'sentinelloop-retrain' (37 runs) only. configs/default.yaml line 36 `max_width: auto`; metrics.json agent_max_width = 82.0 / 77.2 / 111.7 / 80.5, not 60.
findings.recommendation: Regenerate the content plan from the script's strings (or delete the plan) and change 'logged' to 'stored in e0_baseline/*.json'.

findings.title: R15 cites a deck PPTX and recording that do not exist; deck slide 7 has an unfilled placeholder
findings.issue: R15 'Where satisfied' names `round2_deck.pptx`, repo and recorded run; the status PROPOSED is honest, but the column implies files that are absent. round2_deck_content.md line 13 still contains '[filled from e5_decision_vs_rmse/summary.json]'.
findings.evidence: ls submission/ shows CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md, make_round1_slide.py, round1_slide.pdf, round1_slide.png, round1_slide_content.md, round2_deck_content.md only. Slide footer (make_round1_slide.py:190) promises 'public repository + recorded clean-clone run'; the workspace is not a git repository.
findings.recommendation: Mark the three Round 2 artefacts 'to be produced' in the Where column, fill the E5 numbers from the summary (C15 already lists them), and create the repository before the Round 2 window.

reviews.summary: I read the cleaning/feature/target/evaluation/conformal/OOF/anomaly/drift modules, the pipeline, all seven experiment scripts and configs, cross-checked every number in EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md and REPRODUCIBILITY.md against the stored summary.json/metrics.json files, verified fold/calibration/tune-split disjointness and config hashes with one-liners, recomputed regime purity, reproduced the FD003 drift alarm from the stored monitor, and ran the fast test suite (97 passed). No fitted parameter is learned from test data and the OOF folds are engine-disjoint, but the worst problems are that (a) preprocessing/model variants (EMA, regime normalisation, asymmetric CQR) and the monitoring rules were selected by looking at official test-set results while the threat model claims "test used once", (b) the project's own E3 output shows the age-matched drift monitor raising a severe false alarm on 50 untouched FD003 test engines, contradicting the "0 false alarms" claim, and (c) controls the documents cite (tests/test_leakage.py, tuning-id assertions, 5-seed protocol) do not exist in the code. Verdict: the pipeline is leakage-clean at the parameter level but the experimental protocol over-uses the test set and several documented safeguards are unimplemented; the headline RMSEs reproduce, the drop-list line in REPRODUCIBILITY.md does not match the artefacts.

findings.title: Preprocessing and model variants were selected on the official test set; threat model claims test was used once
findings.issue: The decision to disable EMA denoising, keep regime normalisation and keep asymmetric CQR as an option were all made by comparing official test-set RMSE/PICP, i.e. hyperparameter/design selection on the evaluation set. THREAT_MODEL A2 asserts 'test used once for final metrics', which is false.
findings.evidence: configs/default.yaml:8-9: 'ablation showed it lags the degradation signal (FD004 test RMSE 22.5 with alpha 0.3 vs 15.4 without; FD002 18.1 vs 14.8)'. docs/DECISION_LOG.md:18 (D13): 'Ablation on the official test sets: FD004 22.53/22.20 RMSE with alpha 0.3 vs 15.54/15.36 without (max_iter 200/400); FD002 18.10 vs 14.76/14.88'; D14: 'FD004 15.54 vs 17.95 without normalisation'. experiments/e7_ablation.py:1-3 'Reports official test RMSE/PICP' and line 48 writes test_rmse_capped/test_picp per variant; docs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md:93 'EMA ... costs 6.6 RMSE on FD004, so it stays off; asymmetric CQR ... improves FD004 coverage from 0.839 to 0.863 ... (kept as an option)'. docs/THREAT_MODEL_AND_FAILURE_MODES.md:9: 'test used once for final metrics'. The FD002 EMA numbers (18.1 vs 14.8) have no stored artefact at all: experiments/results/e7_ablation/summary.json contains only FD001 and FD004 and gives FD004 with_ema 23.20 vs full 16.61, not 22.5 vs 15.4.
findings.recommendation: State explicitly in REPRODUCIBILITY/THREAT_MODEL that D13/D14 and the E7 table are test-set comparisons; base the EMA/regime/asymmetric decisions on the E7 holdout columns or on OOF CV (both already computed) and keep the official test for one confirmatory run; remove or re-run the unrecorded FD002 EMA numbers.

findings.title: Monitoring rules were iterated against official test engines, and the final 'zero false alarm' numbers are reported on the same engines
findings.issue: The age-matched drift reference (D17), change-relative detection (D19), top_k=2, critical-column and full-range quality rules (D20) were all adopted after observing failures on the official test set (E3 corrupts ds.test; E4 scenario C samples test_f). The E3/E4-drift headline numbers (detection 98-100%, 0 false alarms) are then reported on those same test engines, so for FD001 at least they are in-sample for the rule design.
findings.evidence: docs/DECISION_LOG.md:22 (D17): 'Fast smoke run: whole-population PSI alarmed on all 20 clean test windows'; :24 (D19): 'counting them as false alarms (52%) was wrong'; :25 (D20): 'Fast FD001 diagnostics: early-life range flagged 18% of clean late-life engines ... chosen on a fast FD001 diagnostic BEFORE the full E3 run'. experiments/e3_stress.py:83 'raw = ds.test'; experiments/e4_retrain_gate.py:115 'pool = drift.early_life_rows(test_f, ...)'. docs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md:51 'detected per engine at 98-100% with zero false alarms (the age-matched quality reference removed the 18% false alarms seen in the fast diagnostic)'.
findings.recommendation: Do the diagnostic/design iteration on held-out training engines (the OOF table already exists) and keep the official test engines for a single confirmatory E3/E4 run; at minimum label FD001 E3 and E4-drift results as the design set and FD002-FD004 as confirmatory.

findings.title: Stored E3 output shows a severe false drift alarm on untouched FD003 test engines; docs claim 0 false alarms and attribute every fleet alarm to the fault
findings.issue: The age-matched drift monitor fires 'severe_single_feature' on the early-life rows of the 50 CLEAN (uncorrupted) FD003 test engines in all five fault scenarios. EXPERIMENT_RESULTS reports 'fleet drift alarm: yes (all)' as fault detection and E4 reports '0 false alarms in 20 clean windows on every subset', never mentioning this column.
findings.evidence: All five FD003 rows in e3_stress/summary.json have 'fleet_drift_alarm_clean_early': True (FD001/FD002/FD004 rows: False). Reproduced read-only from artifacts/FD003/drift_monitor.pkl with the E3 seed-42 split: 50 clean engines -> alarm True, reasons ['severe_single_feature'], s9_rm PSI 1.53; all 100 test engines -> alarm False, s9_rm PSI 0.27; the other 50 engines uncorrupted -> alarm False. docs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md:45-49 column 'fleet drift alarm' = 'yes (all)'; :65 '0 false alarms in 20 age-matched clean windows on every subset'. src/sentinelloop/drift.py:106 severe rule 'v > self.severe_psi_threshold'. E4's 20 'clean windows' are 500-row random samples from one pooled early-life frame (e4_retrain_gate.py:117-122), which averages out engine heterogeneity and so cannot see this failure.
findings.recommendation: Report the fleet_drift_alarm_clean_early column and treat FD003 as a false-alarm case; measure false-alarm rate over many random engine subsets of realistic fleet size rather than overlapping row windows; reconsider or raise the single-feature PSI>1 rule for small fleets.

findings.title: Threat-model leakage controls cite a test file and assertions that do not exist
findings.issue: A1 names tests/test_leakage.py as the check that 'feature at cycle t unchanged when future rows are altered; fit objects contain only training ids'; A2 says 'Config records which engine ids were tuning; experiment scripts assert no test ids in tuning'. None of this exists.
findings.evidence: ls tests/test_leakage.py -> 'No such file or directory' (tests/ listing has 28 files, none named test_leakage). grep -n assert experiments/*.py -> no matches. grep tune_units/tuning_units in experiments/results/*/summary.json and artifacts/*/*.json -> no matches; configs contain no engine ids. Causality is partially covered by tests/test_features.py:14 and tests/test_clean.py:34, but no test checks that fitted objects hold only training ids.
findings.recommendation: Either add tests/test_leakage.py (causality + 'fit objects contain only training ids' + 'no test ids in tuning') and store tune/eval engine ids in E1's summary.json, or rewrite rows A1/A2 to describe the checks that actually exist.

findings.title: REPRODUCIBILITY.md drop list contradicts the stored artefacts
findings.issue: The documented sensor drop list does not match what the pipeline and E0 actually dropped.
findings.evidence: docs/REPRODUCIBILITY.md:17: 'FD001/FD003: s1, s5, s6, s10, s16, s18, s19; FD004: s1, s5, s18, s19'. artifacts/FD001/metrics.json and experiments/results/e0_baseline/FD001_metrics.json: dropped_sensors ['s1','s5','s10','s16','s18','s19'] (s6 kept, n_features 62); FD003: ['s1','s5','s16','s18','s19'] (s6 and s10 kept, n_features 66); FD002 (['s1','s5','s18','s19']) is not stated at all.
findings.recommendation: Regenerate the line from metrics.json (FD001: s1,s5,s10,s16,s18,s19; FD003: s1,s5,s16,s18,s19; FD002/FD004: s1,s5,s18,s19).

findings.title: Pre-registered 5-seed protocol was never run; every verdict rests on a single seed-42 split with one-engine effect sizes
findings.issue: The plan and hypotheses commit to 5 seeds reported as mean ± std; the code defines SEEDS but never uses it, so no variance estimate exists for E1/E2/E5/E7 and the frontier conclusions are within single-engine noise.
findings.evidence: docs/EXPERIMENT_PLAN.md:3 'Seeds: 5 (42, 43, 44, 45, 46) wherever randomness exists; reported as mean ± std'; docs/INNOVATION_HYPOTHESES.md:12 '5 seeds where randomness exists'. experiments/common.py:20 'SEEDS = [42, 43, 44, 45, 46]' has no other reference in the repository (grep). Every summary.json is one run with seed 42; e7_ablation.py:3 'one split'. E1 frontier: FD001 C_late_eval 0.0143 = 1/70 engines; 'C better at 2/16, dominated at 2/16' (EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md:24) hinge on differences of 1-2 engines and ~1 cycle of discarded life.
findings.recommendation: Loop E1/E2/E5/E7 over the five seeds (fold, tune/eval and holdout splits), report mean ± std and the number of engines behind each late-rate difference, or delete the 5-seed commitment from the plan and hypotheses and state that results are single-split.

findings.title: OOF tables and all 'held-out' splits share a CleanState fitted on every training engine, so they are not fully out-of-fold
findings.issue: Cleaning statistics (os mean/std, KMeans regimes, per-regime sensor mean/std, drop list) are fitted once on ALL training engines before the fold loop; only model, calibration and anomaly detector are refitted per fold. The same applies to baseline CV, E4 'validation engines (never trained on)' and the E7 holdout. The docstring calls the result 'leakage-free'.
findings.evidence: experiments/common.py:52-56 prepared() -> baseline.prepare_frames(); src/sentinelloop/baseline.py:27 'state = clean.CleanState.fit(train_i, ...)' on the full train; oof.py:23-28 fits only cqr and det per fold on train_f that is already transformed; baseline.py:50-56 same for CV; e4_retrain_gate.py:54,62 splits after prepared(); e7_ablation.py:27-37 fits state on tr (includes hold units). oof.py:4-5: 'The result is a leakage-free cycle-by-cycle prediction table'.
findings.recommendation: Move CleanState.fit (and feature building) inside the fold/holdout loop, or qualify the claim as 'model/calibration out-of-fold; unsupervised scaling fitted on all training engines'. Numerical impact is expected to be small (unsupervised statistics), but the claim should match the code.

findings.title: All engine splits derive from one permutation: E1 tuning engines = deployed model's calibration engines = OOF folds 0-1; E7 holdout = E4 validation = fold 0
findings.issue: tune_eval_split, conformal.split_engines, evaluate.engine_folds, e4 split_units and the E7 holdout all shuffle sorted units with default_rng(42) and take a prefix, so the splits are nested rather than independent. The E1 tuning engines' OOF predictions come only from the fold-0 and fold-1 models, whose conformal calibration differs markedly from folds 2-4, and the thresholds recommended for a fleet are tuned on exactly the engines that calibrate the production interval.
findings.evidence: Verified by one-liner for all four subsets: set(tune_eval_split) == set(conformal.split_engines calibration) is True; tune engines subset of fold0+fold1 val_units is True (FD001: 20 in fold 0, 10 in fold 1). experiments/results/oof/FD001_full_folds.json qhat per fold: 1.47, 0.53, 6.30, 12.01, 5.34; suggested_max_width 90.8, 102.3, 74.1, 119.6, 98.6. Code: common.py:87-92; src/sentinelloop/conformal.py:73-78; src/sentinelloop/evaluate.py:19-27; e4_retrain_gate.py:27-33; e7_ablation.py:35-36. docs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md:28 recommends 'tuned lower-bound thresholds 5-8'.
findings.recommendation: Use a distinct seed offset per split purpose and stratify tuning engines across all folds (e.g. every 3rd engine of each fold) so tuned thresholds are evaluated against the same mixture of fold calibrations; store the engine ids of each split in summary.json.

findings.title: E5 'inversion' criterion is partly satisfied by construction: the lower-bound row carries the point model's RMSE and tied pairs count as inversions
findings.issue: For kind='lower' the RMSE is computed on rows_eval['point'], so 'HGBR + CQR lower bound' has identical RMSE to 'HGBR 70% point' by construction; the inversion loop then compares this tied pair by sort order. The other inversions are 0.3-1.8 cycles of discarded life with late rates tied at 0. H5 is still reported 'SUPPORTED (inversions on 4/4 subsets)'.
findings.evidence: e5_decision_vs_rmse.py:38 'rmse = metrics.rmse(rows_eval["rul"], rows_eval[col] if kind == "point" else rows_eval["point"])'; :54-61 inversion test on sorted RMSE with no minimum effect size. experiments/results/e5_decision_vs_rmse/summary.json FD004 inversion: 'hgbr_70pct_point (rmse 16.05) vs hgbr_cqr_lower_bound (rmse 16.05): late 0.006 vs 0.000'; FD001 inversions are discarded 25.6 vs 25.2 with late 0.000 vs 0.000. docs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md:95,121.
findings.recommendation: Exclude RMSE-tied pairs, require a minimum effect (e.g. >= 2 engines or >= 2 cycles), label the lower-bound row's RMSE as 'point model RMSE', and report H5 as supported only where the inversion is larger than split noise.

findings.title: Batch imputation uses backward fill (non-causal) while stream mode is forward-fill only
findings.issue: clean.impute does ffill then bfill per unit, so a leading missing value at cycle t is filled from a future cycle; CleanStream can only forward-fill. The 'causal' and 'batch == stream' claims therefore hold only when no leading values are missing. No reported number is affected (C-MAPSS has no NaNs; E3 injects missingness only in the last 20 cycles, which ffill covers).
findings.evidence: clean.py:27-28 'out[cols] = out.groupby("unit")[cols].ffill(); out[cols] = out.groupby("unit")[cols].bfill()'; stream.py:28-35 forward-fill only; docs/REPRODUCIBILITY.md:15 states ffill then bfill; THREAT_MODEL A1 claims 'causal rolling/EMA'.
findings.recommendation: Drop bfill in batch (leave leading NaNs or fill with the regime mean) so batch and stream are identical, and add a test that batch cleaning of a frame with a leading NaN equals the stream output.

findings.title: Experiment agent hard-codes 14 sensors for the imputed fraction; pipeline uses the real kept-sensor count
findings.issue: severities_for_engine divides n_imputed by 14.0, but kept sensors are 15 (FD001), 17 (FD002/FD004), 16 (FD003) and pipeline.observation_from_row divides by len(state.kept_sensors). No effect today because OOF n_imputed is always 0, but E2's quality rule would be miscalibrated on data with missingness.
findings.evidence: common.py:110 'imputed_frac=float(imp) / 14.0'; pipeline.py:49-50 '/ max(1, n_sensors)' with n_sensors = len(state.kept_sensors) (pipeline.py:123); metrics.json dropped_sensors lists give 15/17/16/17 kept.
findings.recommendation: Pass n_sensors from the clean state into severities_for_engine.

findings.title: E0 baseline artefacts were produced under a different configuration than the shipped configs
findings.issue: The config_hash stored in each E0 metrics file does not match config.config_hash(config.load(subset)) for the current configs, so the 'config hash in every metrics.json' reproducibility guarantee does not hold for E0. The RMSEs coincide with the pipeline re-run under the current config, so model-relevant keys are evidently unchanged, but this is inferred, not recorded.
findings.evidence: E0 config_hash FD001 32521ec5798c, FD002 49ee491d440a, FD003 cfb02d8ff15d, FD004 9570cc561c5f; current config hashes 83fdcf31e3fd, fd253a160a87, f8eed41381fa, e32edc97c814 (these match artifacts/<subset>/metrics.json and the OOF folds.json). docs/REPRODUCIBILITY.md:11,49.
findings.recommendation: Re-run `python -m sentinelloop baseline --subset all` under the final configs so E0's hash matches, or note which keys changed.

findings.title: 'Cluster purity 100%' is marked VERIFIED but is computed nowhere and stored in no artefact
findings.issue: The purity figure appears in REPRODUCIBILITY.md:16, DECISION_LOG D14, the Round 1 slide and the claim matrix (status VERIFIED), but no code path computes it and no metrics.json records it. I recomputed it read-only: purity is 1.000 on FD002 and FD004 train and test, so the claim is correct but currently unevidenced.
findings.evidence: grep -rn purity --include=*.py -> no hits; metrics.json has no purity key. One-liner with CleanState.fit(n_regimes=6, seed=42) and crosstab against rounded (os1,os2,os3): FD002 train 1.0 / test 1.0; FD004 train 1.0 / test 1.0.
findings.recommendation: Compute regime purity in prepare_frames/run_baseline and write it to metrics.json so the matrix can point at an artefact.

findings.title: Conformal calibration treats correlated within-engine rows as independent and includes pre-warmup cycles absent from the test protocol
findings.issue: Five random cycles per calibration engine (cycle >= 5) are pooled into one score set of size n = 5 x engines for the finite-sample quantile; rows from the same engine are correlated, and cycles 5-19 (rolling window not full, anomaly not armed) never occur in the official test protocol (shortest test trajectory 19-38 cycles). The exchangeability caveat is stated, but measured FD004 coverage is well below nominal.
findings.evidence: conformal.py:108 'cal = evaluate.random_rows_per_engine(cal_rows, n_per_engine=truncations_per_engine, seed=seed)' with evaluate.py:45 default min_cycle=5; conformal.py:85-88 quantile level uses n = len(scores). artifacts/FD004/metrics.json picp_test_capped 0.823 (nominal 0.90); FD002 0.896. Test min lengths (loaded): FD001 31, FD002 21, FD003 38, FD004 19.
findings.recommendation: Sample calibration cycles >= window (20) and either use one conformity score per engine or state that the finite-sample correction assumes row-level exchangeability; report per-subset coverage next to nominal wherever PICP is quoted.

findings.title: Headline RMSE is the all-engine HGBR, not the 70%-engine model the agent actually acts on
findings.issue: The pipeline trains hgbr_all on 100% of training engines for the reported hgbr_rmse_capped (the number on the Round 1 slide) but every decision, interval and E1/E2 replay uses the CQR point/quantile models trained on 70% of engines, whose test RMSE is different. The docs never say which model the headline refers to.
findings.evidence: pipeline.py:94-98 trains hgbr_all and cqr separately; metrics.json: FD001 hgbr_rmse_capped 14.39 vs cqr_point_rmse_capped 14.69; FD002 14.88 vs 15.32; FD003 13.88 vs 13.50; FD004 15.36 vs 15.15. submission/round1_slide_content.md:37 quotes 14.4/14.9/13.9/15.4.
findings.recommendation: State on the slide/deck that the headline RMSE is the all-engine point model and quote the deployed CQR point model's RMSE beside it.

reviews.summary: I verified the PHM08/PICP/MPIW/replay formulas in src/sentinelloop/{metrics,replay,policy,retrain}.py against tests, then cross-checked every number in README.md, docs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md, submission/CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md, round1_slide_content.md (plus the rendered PNG) and round2_deck_content.md against experiments/results/*/summary.json, e0_baseline/*_metrics.json, artifacts/*/metrics.json and the stage logs; the headline per-subset RMSE/PHM08/PICP/MPIW/order/escalation values and the E1–E7 tables all reproduce from the artefacts, and the fast test suite passes (97 tests, 103 collected). The worst problem is that the headline "model performance" RMSE/PHM08 (14.39/336 etc.) belong to an all-engines HGBR that the agent never uses and that is not the MLflow champion; the deployed CQR point model (pipeline.py lines 50/113/160) scores 14.69/15.32/13.50/15.15 RMSE and 378/1112/350/1057 PHM08 (stored as cqr_point_* in artifacts/*/metrics.json), and no document says so. Beyond that, several quoted ranges in the results doc and claim matrix do not match their artefacts (E5 "0.3–1.8 cycles more on every subset" is reversed on FD002 and tied on FD001; the label-corrupted challenger is only 2.66 RMSE worse on FD004, not "4–5"; "33–46 s" vs stored elapsed_s 51–76 s), the PHM08 citation string stamped into every metrics.json swaps the paper's a1/a2, the replay's mean discarded life silently excludes late orders contrary to the pre-registered definition, and a fleet-level drift alarm on clean FD003 data in E3 is unreported; overall the numbers are honest but the prose around them needs a careful correction pass before a judge reads it.

findings.title: Headline RMSE/PHM08 come from a model the agent does not use and that is not the registered champion
findings.issue: README.md lines 11–14, deck slide 5 (round2_deck_content.md line 11) and C1 present 'RMSE capped / raw' and 'PHM08' next to PICP/MPIW as one model's performance. The RMSE/PHM08 are hgbr_rmse_* from `hgbr_all` (trained on all engines, line 94, column point_all_engines) while the agent's rul_point is the CQR point model (line 50: `rul_point=float(row["point"])`, predictions from `cqr.predict` line 113) and the MLflow `champion` alias is `model=cqr.point` (line 160). The model that actually issues work orders scores worse on FD001/FD002.
findings.evidence: artifacts/FD001/metrics.json: hgbr_rmse_capped 14.3857, cqr_point_rmse_capped 14.6865, hgbr_phm08 336.08, cqr_point_phm08 377.71. FD002: 14.8798 vs 15.3177; PHM08 1006.68 vs 1111.91. FD003: 13.8787 vs 13.5014. FD004: 15.3563 vs 15.1530. grep of README.md, docs/*.md, submission/*.md for 'cqr_point' / 'point_all_engines' returns nothing.
findings.recommendation: Either report the CQR point model's RMSE/PHM08 (the deployed/champion model) in the headline table, or add a second column and state explicitly that the all-engines HGBR is a reference model not used by the agent. Make the README table header name the model.

findings.title: E5 'better-RMSE model discards 0.3–1.8 cycles MORE on every subset' is contradicted by the artefact
findings.issue: The stated size of the H5 inversion among point models is wrong in direction and range. On FD002 the better-RMSE pair (hgbr_all 15.98 vs hgbr_70pct 16.24) discards 0.67 cycles LESS, on FD001 one pair is exactly tied, FD003 has a 0.14 pair, and the largest difference is 2.45 (FD002 hgbr_70pct vs RF). The same wording is copied into CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md C15 (line 21) and INNOVATION_HYPOTHESES.md H5 (line 20).
findings.evidence: Recomputed from experiments/results/e5_decision_vs_rmse/summary.json: FD001 +0.41, +0.00, +0.41; FD002 +1.78, +2.45, −0.67; FD003 +1.26, +1.11, +0.14; FD004 +1.46, +1.17, +0.29 (better-RMSE minus worse-RMSE mean_discarded_life).
findings.recommendation: Rewrite as: 'among the three point models, 9 of 12 pairs invert on discarded life by 0.1–2.5 cycles, one pair is tied and one (FD002, hgbr_all vs hgbr_70) goes the other way'. Update C15 and the H5 row identically.

findings.title: 'Label-corrupted challenger RMSE 4–5 worse than the champion' is false for FD004 (2.66)
findings.issue: Secondary E4 finding (a) and CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md C14 (line 20) state the B2 challenger is 'RMSE 4–5 worse than the champion' on all four subsets. The FD004 delta is 2.66.
findings.evidence: experiments/results/e4_retrain_gate_secondary/summary.json B2 rows: FD001 19.84−15.19 = 4.65; FD002 20.90−16.43 = 4.48; FD003 19.11−13.95 = 5.17; FD004 20.63−17.97 = 2.66.
findings.recommendation: Change to 'RMSE 2.7–5.2 worse' in both documents; the rejection conclusion is unaffected.

findings.title: PHM08 citation string swaps the paper's a1/a2 and is stamped into every metrics.json
findings.issue: PHM08_CONVENTION ends 'Saxena et al. 2008 list a1=10, a2=13'. In the paper's notation (as given in the review brief and as cited across the C-MAPSS literature) a1=13 applies to early predictions (d<0) and a2=10 to late (d≥0). The formula on line 26 is correct (early exp(−d/13)−1, late exp(d/10)−1, d = pred − true, late penalised more; test_metrics.py line 16–21 hand-checks it), but the reference note contradicts it and is written verbatim into all eight artifacts/*/metrics.json and e0_baseline/*_metrics.json files under 'phm08_convention'. I could not open the paper itself (not in the repo), so the paper's exact wording is unverified; the string is nevertheless inconsistent with the brief's convention.
findings.evidence: experiments/results/e0_baseline/FD001_metrics.json 'phm08_convention': '... Saxena et al. 2008 list a1=10, a2=13.'
findings.recommendation: Change the string to 'Saxena et al. 2008: a1=13 (early, d<0), a2=10 (late, d≥0)'; regenerate or hand-edit the stored artefacts' convention field, and add 'a1=13' / 'a2=10' to test_phm08_convention_string_is_explicit.

findings.title: '33–46 s per subset' contradicts the elapsed_s stored in the final artefacts (51–76 s)
findings.issue: C18 and deck slide 3 (round2_deck_content.md line 9) claim 'full run 33–46 s per subset' citing full_run_stage1_pipeline.log '(`elapsed_s` in metrics)'. The stage-1 log does say 33.2/46.4/34.6/39.4 s, but the artefact the matrix names as evidence, artifacts/<subset>/metrics.json, records the later (stage 5) run at 51.0/61.9/53.0/76.0 s.
findings.evidence: experiments/results/full_run_stage1_pipeline.log lines 18/26/34/42: 'done in 33.2 s', '46.4 s', '34.6 s', '39.4 s'. artifacts/FD001..FD004/metrics.json 'elapsed_s': 51.0, 61.9, 53.0, 76.0.
findings.recommendation: Quote the range from the artefact that will be shipped (51–76 s, or 'about a minute per subset'), or state that timings vary between runs and cite the log only.

findings.title: Fleet-level drift monitor alarms on CLEAN FD003 data in E3; undisclosed while README says 'zero false alarms'
findings.issue: E3 stores two fleet alarms per row: fleet_drift_alarm_mixed_tail (reported as 'fired on every fault scenario') and fleet_drift_alarm_clean_early, computed in experiments/e3_stress.py line 115 as mon.check on the early-life window of the untouched clean engines. For FD003 it is true on all five fault rows, i.e. the fleet monitor raises an alarm on clean early-life test data regardless of the injected fault. No document mentions it; README.md line 16 and C12 say '... with zero false alarms' (which is only the per-engine rate).
findings.evidence: experiments/results/e3_stress/summary.json: every FD003 row has 'fleet_drift_alarm_clean_early': true; all FD001/FD002/FD004 rows false. e3_stress.py line 115: rep_clean_early = mon.check(early1[early1.unit.isin(clean_units)][mon_cols]).
findings.recommendation: Report the clean-early fleet alarm per subset in the E3 table, explain FD003 (or show its reasons), and qualify 'zero false alarms' as 'per engine' in README, C12 and the deck.

findings.title: Mean discarded life is computed over on-time orders only, contrary to the pre-registered definition and undisclosed in results
findings.issue: decision_metrics sets mean_discarded_life = mean of true_rul_at_order over `on_time` (ordered and not late), so late orders (true RUL 0–4) are dropped, while mean_lead_time (line 57) averages over all orders. docs/EXPERIMENT_PLAN.md line 16 pre-registers 'discarded life = true RUL at first order; lead time = same quantity'. EXPERIMENT_RESULTS never states the exclusion (only tests/test_replay.py line 65 comment 'over on-time orders only'). For the tuned/cost policies with 1–21% late orders this inflates the reported discarded life and makes 'lead time' and 'discarded life' different numbers although the plan says they are the same.
findings.evidence: replay.py line 48: on_time = ordered[~ordered['late']]; line 55 uses on_time; line 57 uses ordered. e1 summary FD001 D_cost_25: late_rate 0.214, mean_discarded_life 8.44 computed over 55 of 70 engines.
findings.recommendation: State the definition in EXPERIMENT_RESULTS E1/E5 and the deck ('over on-time orders'), or report discarded life over all orders and keep a separate on-time figure; reconcile with EXPERIMENT_PLAN.

findings.title: Interval coverage is quoted without saying it is against capped truth; raw-truth coverage is 0.87/0.68/0.80/0.56
findings.issue: README table header '90% interval coverage' and deck slide 5 'PICP' (round2_deck_content.md line 11) give 0.94/0.90/0.91/0.82 with no 'capped' qualifier; only C4 says '(capped truth)'. The artefact also stores picp_test_raw, which is far lower, and README's own convention section says RMSE is 'always reported against ... raw truth' but does not do so for coverage.
findings.evidence: artifacts metrics.json picp_test_capped / picp_test_raw: FD001 0.94 / 0.87; FD002 0.8958 / 0.6757; FD003 0.91 / 0.80; FD004 0.8226 / 0.5565.
findings.recommendation: Label the coverage column 'PICP vs RUL capped at 125' in README and on slide 5, and add the raw-truth coverage (or a footnote) consistent with the capped/raw RMSE convention.

findings.title: 'Cluster purity 100%' has no stored artefact; the cited decision-log row carries stale numbers
findings.issue: C6, the rendered Round-1 slide ('k = 6 for FD002/FD004, cluster purity 100%'), round1_slide_content.md line 15 and deck slide 4 quote 'purity 100%'. No JSON/CSV in artifacts/ or experiments/results/ contains a purity value; the only source is prose in docs/DECISION_LOG.md D14, whose accompanying RMSE pair 'FD004 15.54 vs 17.95 without normalisation' matches neither the E7 artefact (16.61 vs 17.93) nor the headline (15.36).
findings.evidence: grep -rni purity artifacts/FD002/*.json artifacts/FD004/*.json experiments/results → no hits; only docs/DECISION_LOG.md line 19. e7_ablation/summary.json FD004 full 16.6129, no_regime_normalisation 17.9339.
findings.recommendation: Store the regime-vs-operating-condition confusion matrix (or purity) in artifacts/<subset>/ or an experiment summary and cite it; update D14's RMSE numbers to the E7 artefact.

findings.title: Demo script overstates escalation on corrupted inputs ('65–100%'); artefact minimum is 24%
findings.issue: Beat 6 says escalation happens 'on corrupted inputs for 65–100%' of engines. escalation_share_full_corrupted in E3 ranges 0.24–1.0; the single-sensor-bias rows on FD001/FD003 are 0.24–0.38. The claim matrix states it covers demo-script claims.
findings.evidence: experiments/results/e3_stress/summary.json escalation_share_full_corrupted: FD003 bias2s 0.24, bias3s 0.26, FD001 bias3s 0.36, bias2s 0.38, FD004 bias2s 0.65; others 0.66–1.0.
findings.recommendation: Say '66–100% for missing values, noise and regime shift; 24–38% for a single biased sensor on FD001/FD003'.

findings.title: 'PICP 0.80 vs 0.97 is within the noise of 100 validation rows' is an unsupported statistical claim
findings.issue: Finding 1(b) excuses the FD001 false rejection by asserting a 0.80 vs 0.97 coverage gap on 100 rows is 'within the noise'. With n=100 the binomial standard error at p=0.8 is about 0.04, so the 0.17 gap is roughly four standard errors; no artefact or computation supports the statement.
findings.evidence: experiments/results/e4_retrain_gate/summary.json FD001 A: champion_picp 0.97, challenger_picp 0.80; validation rows = 20 engines × 5 = 100 as stated in the doc.
findings.recommendation: Remove 'within the noise' or replace with a computed interval; keep the (valid) point that 100 rows is a small set for an absolute floor.

findings.title: The lower-bound extra discarded life is quoted as '11–17' in one place and '12–17' in another; artefact is 11.3–17.7
findings.issue: E5 finding 2 and C15 say '12–17 cycles more discarded life'; E1 finding 2, C10, deck slide 7 and DEMO_SCRIPT say '11–17'. The artefact gives 17.71 (FD001), 12.91, 11.26, 12.83, so the lower end rounds to 11 and the upper to 18.
findings.evidence: e1_policy_replay/summary.json verdicts discarded_C_T − discarded_A_T: 17.71 / 12.91 / 11.26 / 12.83; identical values in e5 summary (hgbr_cqr_lower_bound − hgbr_70pct_point).
findings.recommendation: Use '11–18 cycles' everywhere (E1, E5, C10, C15, deck slide 7, demo script, H1/H5 rows).

findings.title: Cost-tuned thresholds '12–18 cycles (expensive failures)' wrong: FD003 stays at 10 for every cost ratio

reviews.summary: I read the prior-art document, innovation hypotheses, D11, both submission content files, the rendered Round 1 slide (PNG + generator script), README, demo script, claim-evidence matrix, and cross-checked citations live (Robinson IJPHM 17(1) 2026 and Romano et al. NeurIPS 2019 both verified as real and correctly attributed; Saxena PHM08 is correct) and the E2 artefact against the docs (numbers match). The worst problems are (a) the headline "escalates only untrustworthy cases to a human" on the slide title band, README and deck slide 1, which the project's own E2 result (escalated engines have equal or lower error rates than acted-upon engines on all four subsets) does not support, and (b) the hypotheses document's promise that IntelliTwin is "cited in every deck and README where H1 appears" and its "Not found anywhere" list, neither of which the submission files or the prior-art document's own caveats back up; the Round 2 deck names no prior work at all. Overall the prior-art document itself is careful and never claims "first", but the submission-facing wording drifts beyond it in several places: a Robinson-style design claim when the pipeline defaults to symmetric CQR, an uncited "published gain ≈ 1–2 RMSE" claim, and a stale D11 that still lists "measured escalation (H2)" as the lead differentiator after H2 was rejected.

findings.title: Headline 'escalates only untrustworthy cases to a human' is contradicted by E2 on clean data
findings.issue: The slide title band (also README.md:3 and round2_deck_content.md:7, slide 1) states as a property that the system 'escalate[s] only untrustworthy cases to a human'. The project's own E2 experiment found the opposite on clean data: every clean-data escalation comes from the width rule and the escalated engines have the same or lower error rate than the acted-upon ones, so the escalated cases are not demonstrably the untrustworthy ones. The claim is supported only for injected faults (E3). The claim-evidence matrix even lists 'that abstention removes errors' under 'Claims deliberately NOT made', yet the headline implies exactly that selectivity.
findings.evidence: make_round1_slide.py:63 renders 'escalate only untrustworthy cases to a human'; README.md:3 'escalates only untrustworthy cases to a human'. experiments/results/e2_abstention/summary.json (loaded): FD001 error_rate_acted_upon 0.175 vs error_rate_among_escalated 0.143, relative_reduction -0.019; FD003 0.071 vs 0.071; conclusion 'NOT SUPPORTED' on 0/4; reasons are all 'insufficient_evidence'. docs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md:40 'width-based abstention does not concentrate wrong decisions'. CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md:30 'Claims deliberately NOT made: ... that abstention removes errors'.
findings.recommendation: Reword the thesis on the slide, README and deck slide 1 to what was measured, e.g. 'escalates corrupted, drifted or over-wide-interval cases to a human (input-trust escalation measured in E3; width escalation alone did not reduce decision errors, E2)'. Keep the word 'only' out unless E2 is re-run with a rule that does concentrate errors.

findings.title: 'Cited in every deck and README where H1 appears' is false: IntelliTwin is cited in no submission file
findings.issue: The hypotheses document commits that the closest prior item, sik04 'IntelliTwin', is 'Cited in every deck and README where H1 appears'. H1 (policy replay, E1) appears in README.md:16, round1_slide_content.md:40 / make_round1_slide.py:181-185 and round2_deck_content.md:13 (slide 7), but none of those files mentions IntelliTwin or sik04. The prior-art document's own Section 7 item 3 says IntelliTwin 'must be cited'.
findings.evidence: grep for 'IntelliTwin|sik04' across README.md, PROJECT_STATUS.md, docs/*.md, submission/*.md, submission/*.py, src/sentinelloop/*.py returns only docs/INNOVATION_HYPOTHESES.md:7. research/PRIOR_ART_AND_DIFFERENTIATION.md:268 'That is survivable ... but must be cited.'
findings.recommendation: Either add the IntelliTwin citation (and the RESS decision-metric papers) to README.md's results paragraph and to deck slide 7, or change the hypotheses document to say where it is actually cited. Do not leave a stated commitment that a judge can falsify by opening the deck.

findings.title: 'Not found anywhere' overstates what the prior-art search can support
findings.issue: The bullet '**Not found anywhere:** measured abstention/escalation ...; a decision-stability (churn) metric' is an absolute absence claim. The prior-art document explicitly limits itself to 'was not found in this search' and lists why that is weak: English only, READMEs read but code not, Kaggle poorly indexed, P1/P2/P3/P5/P6/P21 verified from abstracts only, and in particular 'whether P2 already defines a churn metric, is unknown'. The prior-art document's own line 192 ('Stability is the metric no public C-MAPSS repo reports') carries the same overreach against its Section 7.
findings.evidence: INNOVATION_HYPOTHESES.md:9 'Not found anywhere:'. PRIOR_ART_AND_DIFFERENTIATION.md:13 'the combination ... was not found in this search'; :266 'in English only ... Non-English theses and Indian hackathon write-ups are likely under-indexed'; :269 'Whether P1/P2 use C-MAPSS, and whether P2 already defines a churn metric, is unknown'; :271 'READMEs were read, code was not'; :192 'Stability is the metric no public C-MAPSS repo reports'.
findings.recommendation: Replace 'Not found anywhere' with 'Not found in our search (30 web + 7 GitHub queries, English only, READMEs not code)' and add the churn caveat from Section 7.4. Align line 192 of the prior-art document the same way.

findings.title: Round 2 deck names no prior work; the decision metrics it presents are uncredited
findings.issue: Slide 10 says only 'prior art acknowledged (nothing claimed as first)' without naming anything, and slide 7 presents late-order rate and discarded life (the Lee & Mitici 'unscheduled maintenance rate' and 'wasted life' metrics, and the de Pater alarm/safety-factor framing) with no citation. The prior-art document instructs the opposite: 'cite P6, P7 and P1 as the sources' and 'Openly citing Robinson, Mitici, Kamariotis and the TU Delft line ... pre-empts the "this is a reproduction" objection'. A judge who knows the RESS line will read uncredited reuse as a novelty claim.
findings.evidence: round2_deck_content.md:13 (slide 7) and :16 (slide 10) contain no author names; grep 'Mitici|Kamariotis|de Pater|Saxena' over submission/*.md hits only the dataset citation. PRIOR_ART_AND_DIFFERENTIATION.md:218 'cite P6, P7 and P1 as the sources'; :241 'Openly citing Robinson, Mitici, Kamariotis and the TU Delft line shows ...'.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line reference strip to slides 7 and 10: Lee & Mitici RESS 2023 (unscheduled-maintenance rate, wasted life), de Pater et al. RESS 2022 (alarm + safety factor), Mitici et al. RESS 2023 (lower-bound trigger), Kamariotis et al. RESS 2024 (cost per unit time), Robinson IJPHM 2026, IntelliTwin (sik04, 2026).

findings.title: Threat-model mitigation D3 claims citations (Javanmardi 2023, Mitici 2023) that exist nowhere in the submission
findings.issue: The mitigation for 'Over-claiming novelty' is recorded as 'Prior art cited (Robinson 2026, Javanmardi 2023, Mitici 2023)'. Only Robinson is cited in any submission-facing file; Javanmardi appears only in the research document and this threat-model row, Mitici only in the hypotheses document. The mitigation is recorded as done but is not implemented.
findings.evidence: THREAT_MODEL_AND_FAILURE_MODES.md:43. grep 'Javanmardi' over README.md, docs/*.md, submission/* hits only docs/THREAT_MODEL_AND_FAILURE_MODES.md:43; grep 'Mitici' hits only docs/INNOVATION_HYPOTHESES.md:8,16.
findings.recommendation: Either add those citations to the slide/deck (see PA-04) or correct the threat-model row to 'Robinson 2026 cited on the slide; others listed in research/PRIOR_ART_AND_DIFFERENTIATION.md only'.

findings.title: 'Design as in Robinson, IJPHM 2026' overstates the match: Robinson is asymmetric CQR, the pipeline default is symmetric
findings.issue: The slide says the intervals are 'design as in Robinson, IJPHM 2026 — cited, not claimed' (also round1_slide_content.md:22). Robinson's paper (fetched live) pairs gradient boosting with an asymmetric conformalized quantile regression that deliberately weights miscoverage against optimistic estimates. SentinelLoop's pipeline calls fit_cqr without the asymmetric flag, whose default is False, and the deck presents asymmetric CQR only as an ablation option. A judge familiar with the paper will see that the reported numbers do not come from Robinson's design.
findings.evidence: WebFetch of https://www.papers.phmsociety.org/index.php/ijphm/article/view/4724: 'asymmetric conformalized quantile regression ... deliberately weighting miscoverage'. src/sentinelloop/conformal.py:93 'asymmetric: bool = False'; src/sentinelloop/pipeline.py:96 calls fit_cqr with alpha, calib_frac, seed only; configs/default.yaml conformal block (lines 21-24) has no asymmetric key; round2_deck_content.md:11 'asymmetric CQR option (0.839 → 0.863 on the ablation split)'.
findings.recommendation: Change the wording to 'CQR intervals (Romano et al. 2019); Robinson, IJPHM 2026 is the closest published C-MAPSS design, whose asymmetric correction we evaluate as an ablation', or make asymmetric CQR the default so the attribution is accurate.

findings.title: 'Published gain ≈ 1–2 RMSE' for deep models is uncited and inconsistent with the project's own literature notes
findings.issue: The slide's 'Why not an LSTM' bullet asserts a quantitative fact about prior work ('published gain ≈ 1–2 RMSE'; same in round1_slide_content.md:23 and round2_deck_content.md:11). No file in the project cites a source for it; the only origin is a Q&A rehearsal line in the analysis report that also gives no reference. The prior-art document contains no entry supporting it, and other project documents give different figures: KNOWN_LIMITATIONS says deep models reach ≈ 11–13 on FD001 versus ≈ 14 here (up to ~3 points), while the prior-art table records a LightGBM repo beating deep models on 3 of 4 subsets and a 2025 deep model at 16.22 on FD001 (worse than SentinelLoop's 14.39).
findings.evidence: make_round1_slide.py:179; analysis/TELIPORT_S4_case_selection_report.md:355 'published gain is 1–2 RMSE points' (no URL); docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md:13 'published deep models reach ≈ 11–13 RMSE on FD001 versus our ≈ 14'; PRIOR_ART_AND_DIFFERENTIATION.md:160 'mateus-aleixo reports LightGBM 12.12 on FD001 and beating deep models on 3 of 4 subsets'; :111 Sharma 2025 'FD001-FD004 RMSE 16.22/19.29/16.84/19.98'.
findings.recommendation: Cite one concrete source (e.g. a named transformer/CNN paper with its FD001 RMSE) and state the comparison as 'best published deep models ≈ 11–13 on FD001 vs 14.4 here', or drop the number and keep the qualitative argument.

findings.title: D11 still lists 'measured escalation (H2)' as the lead differentiator after H2 was rejected; no later decision re-weights
findings.issue: D11 (status VERIFIED) defines the differentiation claim as 'the measured escalation (H2), the silent-wrong-order stress metric (H3), the decision-metric gate with a visible reject (H4) and rules-plus-alias traceability (H6)'. E2 then returned NOT SUPPORTED on 0/4 subsets and the prior-art document itself said that concentrating escalations on the worst engines 'is what turns "we have a human-in-the-loop flag" into evidence'. No decision after D11 re-weights the differentiation, so the decision log's stated basis for the entry's novelty story is stale and conflicts with the headline wording (PA-01).
findings.evidence: DECISION_LOG.md:26 D11 text; grep 'H2|escalat|differentiat' in DECISION_LOG.md hits only D16 (width threshold) and D11; experiments/results/e2_abstention/summary.json conclusion 'NOT SUPPORTED'; PRIOR_ART_AND_DIFFERENTIATION.md:200 '(c) is what turns "we have a human-in-the-loop flag" into evidence'.
findings.recommendation: Add a decision (D22) recording that after E2 the differentiation rests on H3, H4, H5, H6 and that escalation is presented as an input-trust mechanism (E3) only; propagate the same framing to the slide title and README.

findings.title: Romano et al. 2019 is cited on the slide but absent from the prior-art document that README names as the reference list
findings.issue: The slide cites 'Romano et al. 2019' for CQR. The citation is real and correctly attributed (Romano, Patterson & Candès, 'Conformalized Quantile Regression', NeurIPS 2019, arXiv 1905.03222; conformal.py:8 names all three authors), but research/PRIOR_ART_AND_DIFFERENTIATION.md, which README.md:75 says is where 'Related work [is] cited', has no entry or URL for it. The citation chain the project advertises (every claim traceable to a document) is broken for this reference.
findings.evidence: WebSearch confirms NeurIPS 2019 / arXiv 1905.03222 by Romano, Patterson, Candès. grep 'Romano|Candes' in research/PRIOR_ART_AND_DIFFERENTIATION.md: no match; README.md:75 'Related work cited in research/PRIOR_ART_AND_DIFFERENTIATION.md'.
findings.recommendation: Add Romano, Patterson & Candès (NeurIPS 2019, arXiv 1905.03222) to Section 8 of the prior-art document, and add the Saxena 2008 PHM08 citation details there as a primary (not 'prior research') entry.

findings.title: Prior-art document's own search counts and date disagree with themselves and with the claim matrix
findings.issue: Section 1.1 says '24 queries (listed below)' while Section 1.2 lists 30 numbered queries and Section 7.1 says '30 web queries'. The document header says 'Research date: 2026-10-18' but CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX C21 dates the same search '2026-10-17'. These are the numbers a compliance reviewer would use to judge search diligence.
findings.evidence: PRIOR_ART_AND_DIFFERENTIATION.md:23 '24 queries'; :32-62 items numbered 1-30; :266 '30 web queries'; :5 'Research date: 2026-10-18'; submission/CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md:27 'VERIFIED (30 web queries, 7 GitHub API queries, 17 READMEs, 28 paper pages, 2026-10-17)'.
findings.recommendation: Correct line 23 to 30 and align the date in C21 with the document header.

findings.title: Demo script asserts what competitors build ('the standard student build') though the prior-art document says nothing is known about Season 4 entrants
findings.issue: Beat 2 opens with 'The standard student build is a point RUL estimate with a threshold.' The prior-art document supports only that a point-threshold alert is commonplace in public C-MAPSS repos, and explicitly states that other TELIPORT teams are unknown and the commonplace table is 'a reasonable but unproven model of what entrants will submit'. Spoken to judges who have just seen other entries, an unsupported statement about competitors invites a correction.
findings.evidence: DEMO_SCRIPT.md:9; PRIOR_ART_AND_DIFFERENTIATION.md:273 'nothing is known about other Season 4 teams ... a reasonable but unproven model of what entrants will submit'; :164 'Fixed point-RUL threshold alerts ... Commonplace (this is the "generic agent")'.
findings.recommendation: Say 'the most common pattern in public C-MAPSS repositories is a point RUL estimate with a threshold' and name one or two of the repos the prior-art document verified.

findings.title: Decision-stability (churn) is listed as a not-found differentiator but never shown as a result in the deck
findings.issue: Churn is claimed as a differentiating metric ('a decision-stability (churn) metric' under 'Not found anywhere'; prior-art line 192 'Stability is the metric no public C-MAPSS repo reports'), yet the Round 2 deck plan never presents it (slide 7 lists late orders, discarded life and the frontier only) and the only result is one sentence that churn is 'similar for both families (4.3–5.7)'. A differentiator that is asserted as absent from prior work but not demonstrated reads as a novelty claim without evidence.
findings.evidence: INNOVATION_HYPOTHESES.md:9; PRIOR_ART_AND_DIFFERENTIATION.md:192; round2_deck_content.md:13 (slide 7, no churn); docs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md:26 'Churn ... similar for both families (4.3–5.7)'.
findings.recommendation: Either put the churn numbers per subset and policy on slide 7 (with the Lee & Mitici / de Pater framing cited) or drop churn from the differentiator lists.
