reviews.summary: I read README.md, pyproject.toml, requirements.lock.txt, Makefile (which was edited mid-review at 04:09, findings are against the current version), docs/REPRODUCIBILITY.md, docs/DEMO_RUNBOOK.md, cli/pipeline/data/config/tracking.py, experiments/run_all.py and common.py, .claude/launch.json; ran `doctor` (exit 0: "python 3.12.1 numpy 2.2.6 pandas 2.3.3 scikit-learn 1.7.2 mlflow 3.0.1 streamlit 1.66.0 / data: all 12 C-MAPSS files present in data\raw / archive pcoe_turbofan.zip: checksum OK / archive CMAPSSData.zip: checksum OK / doctor: OK") and `pytest tests -q -m "not slow"` (exit 0, output is only two dot lines "[ 74%]" and "[100%]" with no summary because pyproject addopts already has -q; --collect-only confirms 103 collected / 6 deselected / 97 selected); diffed the lock against `pip freeze` (identical), loaded every metrics.json/summary.json/oof folds.json/retrain_log.json, queried artifacts/mlflow.db read-only, HEAD-checked the S3 URL (200, ETag a83e8f12..., 12,429,152 bytes) and tested pip's behaviour on a non-existent editable path. The worst problem is that requirements.lock.txt line 77 is `-e c:\users\hp\onedrive\desktop\tata`, so README step 2 (`pip install -r requirements.lock.txt`) aborts on any machine other than this laptop (pip refuses the editable requirement before installing anything, verified), and line 69 `pywin32==312` makes it Windows-only despite README claiming macOS/Linux; close behind are that the only recorded `run_all.py` invocation ended `exit=1` (full_run.log) so the "one command reproduces stages 1-6" claim is unsupported, that the "33-46 s per subset (metrics elapsed_s)" claim repeated in REPRODUCIBILITY/CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX/OFFICIAL_REQUIREMENTS contradicts the stored metrics.json (51.0/61.9/53.0/76.0 s), and that the E0 evidence folder is an undocumented hand copy because `baseline` writes to artifacts/<subset>/ and clobbers the pipeline's files. Verdict: same-machine determinism is real (E0 and pipeline HGBR numbers are bit-identical, OOF cache config hashes match the current configs, doctor and tests pass, README/E0 tables match their artefacts), but the entry is not currently installable from its own lock file on a fresh machine, the MLflow store and metrics embed absolute OneDrive paths, and several runtime/ordering claims in the docs are not what the artefacts and logs show.

findings.title: Lock file contains an editable install of this laptop's OneDrive path; README setup fails on any fresh machine
findings.issue: Line 76-77 read `# Editable install with no version control (sentinelloop==0.1.0)` / `-e c:\users\hp\onedrive\desktop\tata`. The lock is a verbatim `pip freeze` (diff against the venv's current `pip freeze` is empty). README line 22, DEMO_RUNBOOK line 8 and Makefile line 14 all run `pip install -r requirements.lock.txt`; pip parses the -e line first and aborts the entire install when the path does not exist, so no dependency is installed and step 3 (`pip install -e . --no-deps`) then yields a package with no numpy/pandas. On Linux/macOS the string is not even a path. DEMO_SCRIPT.md line 30 claims 'Everything you saw is reproducible from a clean clone with the commands in the README'. It also leaks the user name and folder.
findings.evidence: `pip install --dry-run --no-deps -e c:\users\nobody\desktop\tata` -> `ERROR: c:\users\nobody\desktop\tata is not a valid editable requirement. It should either be a path to a local project or a VCS URL`, exit 1. `diff <(sort requirements.lock.txt) <(sort pip-freeze)` -> no differences.
findings.recommendation: Regenerate with `pip list --format=freeze --exclude-editable > requirements.lock.txt` (or `pip freeze --exclude-editable`), delete lines 76-77, keep the explicit `pip install -e . --no-deps` step, and rehearse the README on a machine that is not this laptop before submission.

findings.title: Lock pins pywin32==312 (Windows-only wheels) while README promises Windows, macOS or Linux
findings.issue: `pywin32==312` has no non-Windows distribution, so `pip install -r requirements.lock.txt` on macOS/Linux fails with 'No matching distribution found' (expected from pywin32's wheel set; not executed here). README line 18 header: 'Setup (Windows, macOS or Linux; Python 3.11+)'; line 22 says 'use .venv/bin/python elsewhere'. pywin32 is a transitive Windows-only dependency (docker/mlflow), not needed by the project.
findings.evidence: requirements.lock.txt line 69 `pywin32==312`; README.md line 18 `## Setup (Windows, macOS or Linux; Python 3.11+)`.
findings.recommendation: Use an environment marker (`pywin32==312; sys_platform == "win32"`) or generate the lock with pip-tools/uv so platform-specific pins carry markers; otherwise drop the macOS/Linux claim from the README.

findings.title: The only recorded run_all.py invocation failed (exit=1); 'reproduces stages 1-6 in one command' is unsupported by any log
findings.issue: REPRODUCIBILITY line 63: '`experiments/run_all.py` reproduces stages 1-6 in one command (expect 60-90 minutes...)'; README line 38 and OFFICIAL_REQUIREMENTS R11 (line 60, 'VERIFIED: one command') repeat it. The stored summaries were produced by running the stage scripts by hand, partly concurrently: summary.json `generated` stamps are e3 03:25:50, e1 03:29:23, e2 03:29:30 (while the stage-5 pipeline re-run was writing metrics.json 03:28-03:31), e6 03:31:27, e4 03:36:10, e7 03:38:42, e4_secondary 03:48:58, e5 04:04:02, i.e. 'stage 4' finished after 'stage 6'. run_all.py's own order (e1,e2,e5,e3,e4,e4sec,e6,e7) is also not the recorded order. Nothing shows run_all.py completing.
findings.evidence: experiments/results/full_run.log lines 1-25: `$ ...python.exe -m sentinelloop run --subset FD001` ... `-> exit 0 in 33 s`, `$ ... run --subset FD002`, `[FD002] training point model ...`, `exit=1` (no traceback, no further steps). No log of a completed run_all.py exists under experiments/results/.
findings.recommendation: Run `experiments/run_all.py` once from a clean `artifacts/` and `experiments/results/oof/`, keep the full log, state the wall time measured, and explain the exit=1 (or remove the 'one command' claim from R11/README until it has been observed).

findings.title: '33-46 s per subset (metrics elapsed_s)' contradicts the stored metrics.json (51-76 s)
findings.issue: C18 (line 24): 'full run 33-46 s per subset for the pipeline | VERIFIED | ... (`elapsed_s` in metrics)'. REPRODUCIBILITY line 56 '33-46 s per subset (metrics `elapsed_s`)', OFFICIAL_REQUIREMENTS line 60 and round2_deck_content line 9 repeat it. The artefact the matrix cites says otherwise because the pipeline was re-run in stage 5 (under CPU contention with the concurrent E5 OOF job) and that re-run is what artifacts/ now holds.
findings.evidence: artifacts/FD001..FD004/metrics.json `elapsed_s`: 51.0, 61.9, 53.0, 76.0. full_run_stage5_e4e6e7.log lines 18/26/34/42: 'done in 51.0 s', '61.9 s', '53.0 s', '76.0 s'. The 33-46 s figures exist only in full_run_stage1_pipeline.log lines 18/26/34/42.
findings.recommendation: Quote the values in the shipped metrics.json (or '33-76 s depending on load') and cite the log that actually matches; a judge who opens metrics.json will see the discrepancy immediately.

findings.title: E0 evidence folder is a hand copy; `baseline` writes into artifacts/<subset>/ and overwrites the pipeline's files
findings.issue: REPRODUCIBILITY line 24 presents `experiments/results/e0_baseline/` as the output of `python -m sentinelloop baseline --subset all`, but baseline.py lines 93-95 write `Path(out_dir)/subset/metrics.json` with out_dir defaulting to `artifacts` (cli.py line 82); no code anywhere references `e0_baseline` (grep over src/ and experiments/*.py: zero hits). The `FD00x_metrics.json` files were renamed and copied manually (undocumented step). Worse, `baseline` and `run` write the same names (`metrics.json`, `predictions_test.csv`, `feature_manifest.json`, `clean_state.pkl`, `model_point.pkl`), so running `baseline` after `run` silently replaces the pipeline metrics (PICP/MPIW/escalation disappear) and the pickles that `e3_stress.load_artifacts` (e3_stress.py lines 34-40) and the dashboard read.
findings.evidence: grep -rn e0_baseline src experiments/*.py -> only docs/REPRODUCIBILITY.md:24. baseline.py line 93 `out = Path(out_dir) / subset`, line 95 `(out / "metrics.json").write_text(...)`. experiments/results/e0_baseline/run.log is console output only.
findings.recommendation: Give `baseline` its own output directory (e.g. `experiments/results/e0_baseline/<subset>/` or `artifacts/<subset>/baseline/`) and document the exact command that produces the shipped files.

findings.title: Runbook's 'expected console line' says 37 work orders; the pipeline prints 39
findings.issue: Line 20: 'Expected console lines (FD001, full config...): ... 37 work orders, escalation share 0.15'. pipeline.py line 250 prints `orders {len(all_orders)}` where all_orders = batch + stream orders (37 + 2 with --stream-units 5). README's table column 'work orders' gives the batch-only count (37/89/22/70) while work_orders.json holds 39/92/24/72 (E6 counts 227 = the latter).
findings.evidence: full_run_stage1_pipeline.log line 18: `[FD001] done in 33.2 s: ... orders 39, escalation share 0.15`. artifacts/FD001/metrics.json n_work_orders_batch 37, n_work_orders_stream 2; artifacts/FD001/work_orders.json has 39 entries; e6 summary n_orders 227.
findings.recommendation: Write '37 batch + 2 stream = 39 orders' in the runbook and label the README column 'batch work orders', or print both counts in the console line.

findings.title: MLflow store and metrics.json embed absolute OneDrive paths; registry/artefacts are not relocatable
findings.issue: tracking.py line 22 `art = Path(artifact_root).resolve()` and line 26 `create_experiment(experiment, artifact_location=art.as_uri())`; pipeline.py line 155 builds the tracking URI from `(out_root / 'mlflow.db').resolve()`. The shipped mlflow.db therefore points every run and registered model at `file:///C:/Users/HP/OneDrive/Desktop/tata/artifacts/mlruns`, and every metrics.json stores `mlflow_tracking_uri: sqlite:///C:/Users/HP/OneDrive/Desktop/tata/artifacts/mlflow.db`. The runbook's fallback (line 27 'unzip over the project to restore') and the Round-2 demo of the `champion` alias (line 40) only work at that exact path; `models:/sentinelloop-FD001@champion` resolves to a missing directory elsewhere. A stray empty `mlruns/` folder also sits in the project root (Default experiment `file:///C:/Users/HP/OneDrive/Desktop/tata/mlruns/0`).
findings.evidence: sqlite read-only query on artifacts/mlflow.db, table experiments: (1,'sentinelloop','file:///C:/Users/HP/OneDrive/Desktop/tata/artifacts/mlruns'), (0,'Default','file:///C:/Users/HP/OneDrive/Desktop/tata/mlruns/0'); runs.artifact_uri likewise absolute. artifacts/FD00x/metrics.json `mlflow_tracking_uri` as quoted. `ls -la mlruns` -> empty directory.
findings.recommendation: Use a relative artifact root (set MLFLOW tracking URI relative, or `artifact_location` as a relative `file:` path / `mlflow-artifacts:`), stop writing resolved paths into metrics.json, delete the root mlruns/, and test the MLflow UI from a restored zip at a different path.

findings.title: Whole project, venv, SQLite databases and pickles live inside a OneDrive-synced folder
findings.issue: Project root is C:\Users\HP\OneDrive\Desktop\tata; `.venv` (pyvenv.cfg: `C:\Python312\python.exe -m venv C:\Users\HP\OneDrive\Desktop\tata\.venv`), artifacts/mlflow.db, artifacts/sentinelloop.db, *.pkl and the audit logs are all synced. OneDrive holds file handles and dehydrates files on demand, which produces 'database is locked'/WinError 32 on `audit_path.unlink()` (pipeline.py line 174), on pickle writes and on sqlite commits; the unexplained exit=1 in full_run.log is consistent with such an interruption (cause unverified). The path also leaks into the lock file, metrics.json, mlflow.db and every stage log ('saved C:\Users\HP\OneDrive\Desktop\tata\experiments\results\...').
findings.evidence: .venv/pyvenv.cfg `command = C:\Python312\python.exe -m venv C:\Users\HP\OneDrive\Desktop\tata\.venv`; full_run_stage2_e1e2.log line 33 `saved C:\Users\HP\OneDrive\Desktop\tata\experiments\results\e1_policy_replay`; REPRODUCIBILITY line 5 'Machine used for every number below: Windows 11 laptop'.
findings.recommendation: Move the working copy out of OneDrive (or exclude the folder from sync) before the final evidence run, and strip machine paths from shipped artefacts and logs.

findings.title: No version control: artefacts and MLflow runs cannot be tied to a code state
findings.issue: The project is not a git repository (no .git, no .gitignore; the lock file itself says `# Editable install with no version control`). Consequently no metrics.json, summary.json or MLflow run carries a commit hash, and the 'numbers from the 2026-10-18 run' cannot be matched to the code that produced them; files were still being edited during this review (Makefile mtime 04:09:20, CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX 04:05:04, after the 03:25-04:04 evidence run).
findings.evidence: `Is a git repository: false` (environment); `cat .gitignore` -> No such file; requirements.lock.txt line 76 comment; mtimes listed via os.path.getmtime.
findings.recommendation: `git init`, commit the evidence state, tag it, and record `git rev-parse HEAD` in metrics.json/summary.json and as an MLflow tag; mention the tag in REPRODUCIBILITY.

findings.title: pyproject allows mlflow 2.x but tracking.py uses the MLflow-3-only `name=` keyword
findings.issue: Line 48 `mlflow.sklearn.log_model(est, name="model", registered_model_name=model_name)`; `name` was introduced in MLflow 3.0 (2.x signature is `log_model(sk_model, artifact_path, ...)`). pyproject.toml line 15 declares `mlflow>=2.15,<3.1`, so anyone who installs from pyproject instead of the lock (e.g. after RR-01 forces them to) can get 2.x and the pipeline raises TypeError at the MLflow step (2.x behaviour inferred from its signature, not executed here).
findings.evidence: inspect.signature(mlflow.sklearn.log_model) in the venv (mlflow 3.0.1) lists [..., 'model_id', 'name'] with `artifact_path` first; pyproject.toml line 15 `"mlflow>=2.15,<3.1"`.
findings.recommendation: Pin `mlflow>=3.0,<3.1` in pyproject (the README troubleshooting already assumes MLflow 3.0 + SQLAlchemy 2.0).

findings.title: OOF caches are reused by filename only; config_hash is recorded but never checked, and run_all.py re-reads rather than recomputes E1/E2/E5
findings.issue: `oof_table` returns the cached `experiments/results/oof/<subset>_full[_bl].csv` whenever the file exists (`if path.exists() and meta.exists() and not force`); the `config_hash` stored in `_folds.json` (line 82) is never compared with the current config. With the 47 MB cache shipped, `run_all.py` does not recompute anything for E1, E2 or E5, and a judge who edits configs/*.yaml and re-runs gets silently stale summaries. Today the hashes match, so the shipped numbers are consistent.
findings.evidence: oof/<subset>_full_folds.json config_hash 83fdcf31e3fd / fd253a160a87 / f8eed41381fa / e32edc97c814 == config.config_hash(config.load(subset)) for all four subsets (MATCH). common.py line 66 has no hash comparison.
findings.recommendation: Compare the stored config_hash (and the pipeline's data hashes) with the current ones and recompute on mismatch; state in REPRODUCIBILITY that run_all.py with the cache present re-reads E1/E2/E5.

findings.title: No thread pinning; cross-machine bitwise reproducibility of HGBR/KMeans not controlled, and troubleshooting tells users to edit models.py
findings.issue: HistGradientBoostingRegressor (models.py lines 33, 38), KMeans (clean.py line 64) and IsolationForest run on OpenMP/joblib pools; no OMP_NUM_THREADS or threadpoolctl control exists anywhere (grep: only the hard-coded `n_jobs: int = 4` for RandomForest at line 42). REPRODUCIBILITY line 37 concedes '±0.5 RMSE and ±20% PHM08 across machines'. README line 71 tells a judge to 'reduce n_jobs in models.py', i.e. to patch source code. Same-machine determinism is verified (E0 and pipeline HGBR RMSE both 14.385660553176727); cross-thread-count bitwise reproducibility is unverified.
findings.evidence: models.py line 42-43; grep -rn 'threadpool|OMP_NUM|set_num_threads' src experiments -> none; artifacts/FD001/metrics.json hgbr_rmse_capped 14.385660553176727 == experiments/results/e0_baseline/FD001_metrics.json hgbr_rmse_capped.
findings.recommendation: Pin thread counts with threadpoolctl (already in the lock) or OMP_NUM_THREADS inside pipeline.run/baseline.run_baseline, expose n_jobs in configs/default.yaml, and state the ±0.5 RMSE tolerance next to every headline number in the claim matrix.

findings.title: Python version guidance is inconsistent and unbounded
findings.issue: README line 18 and DEMO_RUNBOOK line 3 say 'Python 3.11+'; REPRODUCIBILITY line 4 says 'Python 3.12.1'; pyproject `requires-python = ">=3.11"` has no upper bound and doctor only checks `>= (3, 11)`. The lock pins numpy 2.2.6 / scipy 1.18.1 / pandas 2.3.3 / pywin32 312, whose wheel availability for the newest CPython is unverified; a judge on 3.14 may be pushed into source builds.
findings.evidence: pyproject.toml line 9; cli.py line 16; .venv/pyvenv.cfg version = 3.12.1.
findings.recommendation: State the tested interpreters explicitly (3.12.1 verified) and set `requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.14"` or test 3.11/3.13 and say so.

findings.title: Doubled -q hides the pass/fail count; '103 passed' was inferred from dots
findings.issue: addopts `-q -p no:cacheprovider` plus the documented `pytest tests -q` (README line 39, REPRODUCIBILITY line 46/61, DEMO_RUNBOOK line 48) runs at -qq, which prints no 'N passed' line. My run and test_full_phase5.log consist only of dot lines; REPRODUCIBILITY line 61 '103 passed, exit 0' is a dot count.
findings.recommendation: Drop `-q` from addopts (or from the documented commands) so the summary line is visible in logs a judge reads.

findings.title: CLI prints a wrong audit-log path and all defaults are cwd-relative without saying so
findings.issue: Line 62 prints `audit log {out_dir}/audit/decisions.jsonl`, but pipeline.py line 172 writes `decisions_{subset}.jsonl` (the wrong path is reproduced in full_run.log line 20). Defaults `data/raw`, `artifacts`, `configs` (lines 81-83) and the dashboard's `experiments/results` are relative to the current directory; nothing says commands must run from the project root.
findings.evidence: cli.py line 62; pipeline.py line 172; full_run.log line 20.
findings.recommendation: Fix the message and resolve defaults relative to the package/project root (as experiments/common.py already does with ROOT).

findings.title: Experiment summaries and E0 metrics lack provenance fields (seed, config_hash, dependent pipeline run)
findings.issue: `save()` adds only `generated`; e3/e6 summaries have no `fast` flag, none has seed, config_hash or the mlflow_run_id of the artefacts they consumed. E0 metrics (baseline.py lines 74-79) record no seed (the dict has no `seed` key) although REPRODUCIBILITY line 6 promises seeds everywhere. E3 (generated 03:25:50) consumed pickles from the stage-1 pipeline, which was then overwritten by the 03:28-03:31 re-run, so the E3 summary cannot be linked to the shipped pickles except by assuming determinism.
findings.evidence: summary.json top keys printed: e3_stress ['hypothesis','table','by_fault','reasons','conclusion','generated']; e0_baseline/FD001_metrics.json has no 'seed' key; artifacts/FD001/metrics.json mtime 03:28:10 local vs e3 generated 03:25:50.
findings.recommendation: Have save() record seed, config_hash per subset, data hashes and the pipeline run_id/metrics.json hash it depended on.

findings.title: Experiments divide imputed count by a hard-coded 14 sensors; pipeline uses len(kept_sensors)
findings.issue: `imputed_frac=float(imp) / 14.0` in severities_for_engine, used by E1/E2/E5, while pipeline.py line 122 uses `n_sensors = len(state.kept_sensors)` (17 on FD004 per REPRODUCIBILITY line 17, which drops only s1,s5,s18,s19). The replayed quality rule therefore differs from the pipeline's on FD002/FD004, so the experiments do not reproduce the deployed agent's quality threshold exactly on the multi-regime subsets.
findings.evidence: experiments/common.py line 110; src/sentinelloop/pipeline.py line 122; docs/REPRODUCIBILITY.md line 17 drop lists.
findings.recommendation: Pass the subset's kept-sensor count from the prepared CleanState instead of the literal 14.0.

findings.title: Shipped mlflow.db mixes smoke/fast runs with the evidence run; champion alias history is not interpretable
findings.issue: The demo (line 40) shows 'registered model sentinelloop-FD001 with the champion alias', but the shipped database holds 49 runs and 6 versions of sentinelloop-FD001 plus 16 of sentinelloop-FD001-gated, accumulated from fast smoke runs and repeated E4 runs; full_run.log line 16-17 shows version 4 being created by the failed run_all attempt. A judge opening the MLflow UI cannot tell which version corresponds to the reported numbers.
findings.evidence: sqlite: `select count(*) from runs` -> 49; model_versions grouped: sentinelloop-FD001 6, sentinelloop-FD001-gated 16, FD002/3/4 2 each, -gated 7 each.
findings.recommendation: Delete artifacts/mlflow.db before the final evidence run so the registry contains exactly the runs cited, and tag runs with the stage/log name.

findings.title: Windows-only tooling paths in launch config and Makefile variable cannot be overridden
findings.issue: launch.json line 6 `runtimeExecutable: ".venv/Scripts/python.exe"` is Windows-only. Makefile lines 2-7 set `PY ?=` and then unconditionally `PY :=`, so `make PY=python3` is ignored, and `make venv` (line 14) relies on whatever `python` is on PATH. (The Makefile was edited at 04:09:20 during this review; the earlier version also contained replay/stress/retrain/stream targets for CLI subcommands that do not exist. Those are gone now.)
findings.evidence: Makefile lines 2-7 and 14 (current version, mtime 2026-10-18 04:09:20); `python -m sentinelloop replay --help` -> 'invalid choice: replay (choose from doctor, data, baseline, run, audit, dashboard)'.
findings.recommendation: Use only the ifeq block for PY (drop the `?=`/`:=` pair), call `$(PY)` consistently, and note that launch.json is for the Windows dev box.

reviews.summary: I read the runbook, script, dashboard/viewdata/cli code, launch.json and every stored artefact the demo touches (artifacts/FD00x/*.json|csv, audit logs, retrain logs, experiments/results/*/summary.json, stage logs, mlflow.db read-only) and executed only read-only checks (doctor, audit, pytest, Arrow-serialisation of every dashboard table). The worst problem is that the scripted demo itself destroys its own evidence: step 3.2 runs the FAST pipeline into the default artifacts/ directory, overwriting the full-run FD001 metrics/decisions/audit log and moving the MLflow champion alias to a fast model before the dashboard is opened, so every number the presenter is told to say (RMSE 14.39, PICP 0.94, 37 orders, 510 audit records) no longer matches the screen, while the retraining-log beat on FD001 has no PROMOTE row at all and the CRITICAL-engine stream replay the script promises cannot be shown because only units 1-5 are streamed. The dashboard code paths do not throw on the present artefacts (all tables Arrow-serialise, replay_check keys match, pytest 97 passed in 25 s), but the demo as written will contradict itself on stage, the reset/fallback plan deletes evidence it cannot regenerate, and the "recorded run in the annex" does not exist.

findings.title: Scripted demo step 2 overwrites the full-run artefacts and moves the champion alias before the dashboard beats
findings.issue: Step 3.2 runs `python -m sentinelloop run --subset FD001 --fast --stream-units 3` with the default `--out-dir artifacts`. pipeline.run writes to artifacts/FD001 (pipeline.py lines 82-84, 191, 221-249), unlinks and recreates artifacts/audit/decisions_FD001.jsonl (lines 172-175) and registers the fast model with `alias="champion"` (line 160). Steps 3.3-3.5 then open the dashboard, audit and MLflow on these fast artefacts, while the script (Beat 7 '0.94 on FD001', Beat 4 '3,409 decisions') and the runbook's own expected lines (line 20: 'RMSE 14.39 capped / 15.53 raw, PHM08 336, PICP 0.94, MPIW 65, 37 work orders') quote the FULL run. The pre-demo check on line 50 ('artifacts/ from a full (not fast) run present') is violated by the runbook's own step 2. The set of CRITICAL engines and work orders may also change with the fast model (unverified), so a pre-chosen engine number can disappear.
findings.evidence: experiments/results/smoke_fast_fd001_v3.log line 17-18 (fast run, same command family): 'max_width 102.3' and 'done in 14.4 s: HGBR RMSE 14.58 capped / 15.81 raw, PICP 0.930, MPIW 81.9, orders 21, escalation share 0.14' versus artifacts/FD001/metrics.json (full): hgbr_rmse_capped 14.3857, picp_test_capped 0.94, mpiw_test 65.10, agent_max_width 81.96, n_work_orders_batch 37, audit_records 510. After a 3-unit fast run the FD001 audit log would hold 100 + 31 + 49 + 126 = 306 records, not 510. mlflow.db registered_model_aliases currently: ('champion', 6, 'sentinelloop-FD001') where version 6 = run a9e6712863f2 tagged fast=False; a demo fast run creates version 7 tagged fast=True and takes the alias.
findings.recommendation: Run the live fast command with a separate output directory (e.g. `--out-dir artifacts_demo --no-mlflow`) or drop the live run and show the stage-1 log instead; open the dashboard on the frozen full-run `artifacts/`; update line 20 and the script so the spoken numbers are the ones on screen; add the out-dir rule to the pre-demo checklist.

findings.title: The CRITICAL-engine stream replay the script promises cannot be shown: only engines 1-5 are streamed and none is CRITICAL
findings.issue: Beat 4 and runbook line 34 say: pick a CRITICAL engine ... then 'the stream replay table (cycle-by-cycle decisions)'. pipeline.py line 200 streams `sorted(ds.test['unit'].unique())[:stream_units]`, i.e. units 1-5 (1-3 with `--stream-units 3`). dashboard.py lines 88-91 render the stream table only if the selected unit has stream rows. On FD001 units 1,2,5 are NONE and 3,4 MEDIUM; the CRITICAL units are 20,31,34,35,42,49,56,66,68,76,81,82. Same on FD004 (stream units 1-5 are MEDIUM/NONE; CRITICAL starts at unit 8). The presenter must choose between a CRITICAL engine and a stream table; the script asks for both on one screen.
findings.evidence: artifacts/FD001/decisions_stream.csv unit values = [1,2,3,4,5]; artifacts/FD001/decisions_test.csv severity for units 1-5 = NONE, NONE, MEDIUM, MEDIUM, NONE; CRITICAL units = [20,31,34,35,42,49,56,66,68,76,81,82]. Same pattern in artifacts/FD004 (stream units 1-5 = MEDIUM, MEDIUM, NONE, NONE, NONE).
findings.recommendation: Either add a `--stream-units-list` option (or stream the N most severe units) and regenerate the frozen artefacts, or rewrite Beat 4 to show the stream replay on unit 3 or 4 (MEDIUM) and the interval/decision panel on a named CRITICAL unit (e.g. FD001 unit 34: lower 0.66, point 6.5, true RUL 7) as two explicit sub-steps.

findings.title: Beat 5 and the runbook promise PROMOTE rows and an 'accepted challenger' on FD001; the FD001 retraining log and registry contain only REJECTs
findings.issue: The script says 'A challenger trained on more data is promoted when it is no worse on validation ... Show the retraining log rows (PROMOTE / REJECT with reasons) and the MLflow aliases'; runbook line 36 promises 'the retraining log with the PROMOTE and REJECT rows' and line 40 'champion, accepted challenger, rejected challenger'. The demo subset is FD001, whose retrain_log.json has no PROMOTE row in either run (A_accept_more_data REJECT 'picp 0.800 < 0.85' and 'picp 0.835 < 0.85'). PROMOTE rows exist only on FD002-FD004. The on-screen E4 caption also reads 'Pre-registered criterion: NOT SUPPORTED'. The spoken 'two better-RMSE challengers' rejected by the floor is three in the artefacts (FD001 primary 16.70 < 16.75, FD001 secondary 15.01 < 15.19, FD004 secondary 16.09 < 17.97).
findings.evidence: artifacts/FD001/retrain_log.json: decisions = REJECT (A, primary), REJECT (B), REJECT (A, secondary), REJECT (B), REJECT (B2); no 'PROMOTE' string in the file. experiments/results/e4_retrain_gate/summary.json table rows 0-1 (FD001) both decision 'REJECT'; conclusion '4/8 scenario outcomes as expected ... NOT SUPPORTED'; secondary '7/12 ... NOT SUPPORTED'. mlflow.db aliases for 'sentinelloop-FD001-gated': champion=13, challenger=16 (the challenger was rejected).
findings.recommendation: Switch the sidebar to FD002 or FD003 for this beat (both have PROMOTE on A and REJECT on B2) or say explicitly 'on FD001 the floor rejected the better challenger; on FD002-FD004 it was promoted'; change 'two' to 'three (FD001 twice, FD004 once)'; rehearse the answer to 'why does the screen say NOT SUPPORTED?'.

findings.title: The reset procedure deletes evidence the demo needs (retrain logs, gated registry, FD002-FD004) and the documented recovery does not regenerate it
findings.issue: Section 2 runs `shutil.rmtree('artifacts')` then a fast FD001 run and claims a 'known clean state in < 1 minute'. That removes artifacts/FD001/retrain_log.json (written only by experiments/e4_retrain_gate.py, line 138), artifacts/mlflow.db (the `sentinelloop-retrain` experiment and all `-gated` registered models shown in step 3.5), and FD002-FD004. Line 27 says the full-quality artefacts come back by 're-run step 1 (≈ 5 min)', but step 1 (`sentinelloop run`) never writes retrain_log.json or the gated registry; only `run_all.py` / `e4_retrain_gate.py` do, which took about 11 minutes for both E4 runs. The 'zipped copy of a good artifacts/' that section 2 and section 4 rely on does not exist under the project root. On Windows, rmtree with ignore_errors=True silently leaves mlflow.db/sentinelloop.db behind if the dashboard or MLflow UI still holds them open, giving a half-reset state.
findings.evidence: grep 'retrain_log' src/sentinelloop/*.py experiments/*.py: only viewdata.py (read) and experiments/e4_retrain_gate.py:138 (write). E4 timestamps in summary.json: primary 03:32:18 -> 03:36:09, secondary 03:42:01 -> 03:48:57. `find . -maxdepth 2 -name '*.zip'` (excluding .venv) returned nothing; `ls *.zip` -> 'No such file'. mlflow.db experiments table: (2, 'sentinelloop-retrain', ...) and 8 registered models incl. 'sentinelloop-FD001-gated'.
findings.recommendation: Create the zip now (artifacts/ + experiments/results/) and record its SHA256 in the runbook; make the reset procedure 'unzip the frozen copy' rather than 'delete and fast-run'; never rmtree while the dashboard/MLflow UI is open; state honestly that retrain_log.json needs e4_retrain_gate.py (~11 min).

findings.title: The presenter is told to say 'the recorded run is in the annex' but no recording exists
findings.issue: The closing line asserts a recorded run in the annex; the runbook's last-resort fallback (line 45) is `submission/recording_*.mp4` 'to be made in Phase 8', and round2_deck_content.md line 18 says it is 'to be made by the team'. If the demo day arrives without it, the closing statement is false and the no-projector/no-machine fallback has nothing behind it.
findings.evidence: `ls -la submission/` lists only CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md, make_round1_slide.py, round1_slide.pdf, round1_slide.png, round1_slide_content.md, round2_deck_content.md; no .mp4 file anywhere in submission/.
findings.recommendation: Record the clean-clone run before the submission deadline (screen capture of doctor -> run -> dashboard -> audit), label it as a recording in the first frame, add its filename and SHA256 to the runbook; until then delete the 'recorded run' sentence from the script.

findings.title: Engine tab prints 'escalation `nan`' for every non-escalated engine, including all 12 CRITICAL ones
findings.issue: The latest-decision line uses `d.iloc[0]['reasons'] or '-'`. decisions_test.csv stores an empty string for non-escalated engines, which pandas reads as float NaN; NaN is truthy in Python, so the markdown shows 'escalation `nan`' instead of '-'. Every CRITICAL engine the script asks the presenter to pick is non-escalated on FD001, so the judge sees 'nan' next to 'R_CRITICAL'.
findings.evidence: Executed: `repr(float('nan') or '-')` -> 'nan'; loading artifacts/FD001 via viewdata and rendering the line for unit 34 gives 'escalation `nan`'. decisions_test.csv: reasons NaN for 85 of 100 engines; all 12 CRITICAL rows have reasons NaN and escalate False.
findings.recommendation: Use `pd.isna(x) or not x` (or `str(x) if isinstance(x, str) and x else '-'`); alternatively read the CSV with `keep_default_na=False` for the reasons column.

findings.title: Experiments tab cannot show the E1 'frontier table' the script calls for, and shows 'NOT SUPPORTED' captions three times during the 'measured evidence' beat
findings.issue: The tab renders only `summary['table']` and `summary['conclusion']` (lines 116-121). E1's `frontier` key (16 rows: target_late_rate, A/C thresholds, discarded life, C_better_or_equal, C_dominated) is never rendered, yet Beat 5 says 'Show the frontier table'. E6 has no `table` key, so 'E6 audit' is a one-line caption. The captions that ARE shown read 'H1 ... NOT SUPPORTED', 'H2 ... NOT SUPPORTED', 'H4 ... NOT SUPPORTED' while the presenter talks about 'the measured evidence for the key claims'; the script prepares the presenter only for H2.
findings.evidence: experiments/results/e1_policy_replay/summary.json keys: ['hypothesis','table','frontier','verdicts','conclusion','fast','generated']; frontier[0] = {'subset':'FD001','target_late_rate':0.0,'A_threshold':12.0,...,'C_better_or_equal':False,'C_dominated':False}. e6_audit_check/summary.json has no 'table' key (DataFrame shape (0,0)). Conclusions quoted from e1, e2, e4 summary.json all end in 'NOT SUPPORTED'.
findings.recommendation: Render `frontier` (and `by_fault`, `replay`) when present; or in the script replace 'Show the frontier table' with 'point at the C_lower_T vs A_point_T rows'; add one sentence in Beat 5 owning H1/H4 'NOT SUPPORTED' before a judge reads it.

findings.title: Runbook 'expected console lines' do not match what the CLI prints (orders 39 not 37; PHM08 never printed; audit path wrong)
findings.issue: Line 20 says the console shows 'PHM08 336, ... 37 work orders'. pipeline.py line 250 prints `orders {len(all_orders)}` = batch 37 + stream 2 = 39 and does not print PHM08 at all. cli.py line 62 then prints 'audit log artifacts/audit/decisions.jsonl', a file that does not exist (logs are per subset, decisions_FD001.jsonl). A judge following the runbook against the terminal sees three discrepancies in the first minute.
findings.evidence: experiments/results/full_run_stage5_e4e6e7.log line 18: '[FD001] done in 51.0 s: HGBR RMSE 14.39 capped / 15.53 raw, PICP 0.940, MPIW 65.1, orders 39, escalation share 0.15'. metrics.json: n_work_orders_batch 37, n_work_orders_stream 2. `ls artifacts/audit/` -> decisions_FD001.jsonl ... decisions_FD004.jsonl, no decisions.jsonl.
findings.recommendation: Change line 20 to 'orders 39 (37 batch + 2 stream)' and drop PHM08 from the console expectation (or print it in pipeline.py line 250); fix cli.py line 62 to print `audit/decisions_<subset>.jsonl`.

findings.title: The 'five log lines' of the live run are interleaved with 13 lines of MLflow/alembic INFO and WARNING noise
findings.issue: Beat 3 tells the presenter to 'Read the five log lines aloud'. With MLflow enabled (the default), the run prints alembic migration INFO lines, 'WARNING mlflow.models.model: Model logged without a signature and input example', and 'Registered model sentinelloop-FD001 already exists. Creating a new version' between pipeline lines 3 and 4. A judge sees a WARNING and a model-registry side effect during a beat that is sold as 'one command, offline, no LLM'.
findings.evidence: experiments/results/smoke_fast_fd001_v3.log lines 4-16 (13 lines) between '[FD001] fitting anomaly detector...' (line 3) and '[FD001] running the Triage Agent...' (line 17); identical pattern in full_run_stage1_pipeline.log lines 4-16.
findings.recommendation: Run the live command with `--no-mlflow` (also avoids DR-01's alias move), or set `logging.getLogger('mlflow').setLevel(logging.ERROR)` and `alembic` to WARNING in tracking.py and log the model with an input_example.

findings.title: Runbook timing claims are not backed by the logs (6x overstated pipeline time; no estimate for the 30-90 minute experiments step)
findings.issue: Line 3 and line 27 say the pipeline takes '≈ 5 min for FD001, ≈ 25 min for all four subsets'; the logs show 33-51 s for FD001 and about 4 min for all four. Line 18 (`experiments/run_all.py --skip-pipeline`) carries no time at all although it is part of 'produce the artefacts the demo shows'; the stage-4 log shows E5 alone took 2,016 s and REPRODUCIBILITY.md line 63 says 60-90 minutes. The doctor (10 s) and audit (5 s) claims are fine: measured 4.5 s and 1.2 s.
findings.evidence: full_run_stage1_pipeline.log: '[FD001] done in 33.2 s', FD002 46.4 s, FD003 34.6 s, FD004 39.4 s; metrics.json elapsed_s = 51.0, 61.9, 53.0, 76.0 (sum 242 s). full_run_stage4_e5.log: OOF 232 s + 746 s + 265 s + 773 s. Measured with Measure-Command: doctor 4.5 s wall, audit 1.2 s wall.
findings.recommendation: Replace '≈ 5 min / ≈ 25 min' with '≈ 1 min / ≈ 4-5 min' and add '≈ 60-90 min (uses the oof/ cache if present)' to line 18 so the team does not discover this on demo morning.

findings.title: Spoken ranges in Beats 5 and 6 do not match the E1/E3 summary.json exactly
findings.issue: (a) 'silent-wrong-order rate went from 2-19% to zero': the naive rate is already 0.0 on three of the 20 rows (FD001 regime_shift, FD003 missing20, FD003 regime_shift), so the honest range is 0-19%. (b) Beat 6 'on corrupted inputs for 65-100%': escalation_share_full_corrupted ranges 0.24-1.00 across the table (0.66-1.00 only for the three passing faults; bias rows 0.24-0.89). (c) Beat 5 E1 '11-17 more cycles': FD001 is 42.89-25.17 = 17.7, i.e. 11-18. (d) 'A single biased sensor is only caught at fleet level': per-engine detection of bias is 88-96% on FD002/FD004; it is only on FD001/FD003 (4-20%) that fleet level is the sole catch.
findings.evidence: e3_stress/summary.json table: silent_wrong_order_naive = 0.0 for rows (FD001, regime_shift), (FD003, missing20), (FD003, regime_shift); escalation_share_full_corrupted min 0.24 (FD003 bias2s), 0.66 (FD003 noise3s); detection_rate bias2s = 0.12, 0.884, 0.04, 0.96. e1_policy_replay/summary.json table: mean_discarded_life C_lower_T 42.886 vs A_point_T 25.171 on FD001 (diff 17.7), FD002 12.9, FD003 11.3, FD004 12.8.
findings.recommendation: Say '0-19%', '66-100% for the three detectable faults, 24-89% for a biased sensor', '11-18 cycles', and 'on the single-regime subsets a biased sensor is caught only at fleet level'.

findings.title: Beat 4 quotes '3,409 decisions' while the FD001 Audit tab shows 510 (or 306 after the demo's fast run)
findings.issue: The Audit tab is per subset (dashboard.py line 124-125 prints 'records: {len(b.audit)}'); 3,409 is the four-subset total from E6. If the presenter says 3,409 while the screen says 510, a judge will ask which is right.
findings.evidence: artifacts/FD001/metrics.json audit_records 510; `python -m sentinelloop audit` output: n 3409 = 510 + 971 + 897 + 1031.
findings.recommendation: Say '510 on this subset, 3,409 across all four, zero mismatches', and run `python -m sentinelloop audit` (1.2 s) right after the click to show the 3,409.

findings.title: `sentinelloop dashboard` launches Streamlit without headless/usage-stats flags; on a machine without ~/.streamlit/credentials.toml it blocks on the e-mail prompt
findings.issue: cmd_dashboard calls `streamlit run dashboard.py -- --out-dir ...` with none of the flags launch.json uses (`--server.headless true --browser.gatherUsageStats false`). On a fresh machine Streamlit's first run prints a 'Welcome to Streamlit ... Email:' prompt and waits; the runbook (line 3) says the demo can run on 'any machine with Python 3.11+'. On the team laptop the prompt will not appear because the credentials file already exists.
findings.evidence: .claude/launch.json runtimeArgs include '--server.headless','true','--browser.gatherUsageStats','false'; cli.py line 76 passes only '--', '--out-dir'. `ls ~/.streamlit` on this laptop: credentials.toml (Jan 23 2026) present.
findings.recommendation: Add `--browser.gatherUsageStats false` (and optionally `--server.headless true` plus an explicit `webbrowser.open`) in cmd_dashboard, or ship a `.streamlit/config.toml` in the repo; add 'credentials.toml present' to the pre-demo checklist.

findings.title: The 8-minute script has zero slack: beats sum to exactly 480 s with the 30 s live run, dashboard start-up, a 100-item engine dropdown and the audit click unbudgeted
findings.issue: 45+60+60+90+120+60+45 = 480 s. Beat 3's 60 s includes the ≈ 30 s run (14.4 s compute plus interpreter/MLflow start-up); Beat 4 requires opening Streamlit (cold start), finding a CRITICAL unit in `st.selectbox('Engine', units)` (default unit 1; the script names no unit number) and switching three tabs; the MLflow UI step is 'optional' but referenced in Beat 5 ('and the MLflow aliases').
findings.evidence: docs/DEMO_SCRIPT.md beat headers (45 s, 60 s, 60 s, 90 s, 120 s, 60 s, 45 s); dashboard.py line 70 `st.selectbox('Engine', units)` over 100 units with no severity hint; smoke_fast_fd001_v3.log 'done in 14.4 s' for the fast run.
findings.recommendation: Name the engine in the script (from the frozen artefacts), pre-open the dashboard and MLflow UI in background tabs before Beat 1, and cut Beat 5 to 90 s to leave 30 s of slack.

findings.title: Fallback 'unzip over the project' breaks MLflow links on any other path, and the whole demo tree lives under OneDrive
findings.issue: mlflow.db stores absolute artifact locations (file:///C:/Users/HP/OneDrive/Desktop/tata/artifacts/mlruns, and the Default experiment at .../tata/mlruns/0 outside artifacts/), and metrics.json stores `mlflow_tracking_uri` with the same absolute path. Restoring the zip on a different machine or folder makes step 3.5's model-version artifact links dangle. Running SQLite databases and multi-MB pickles inside a OneDrive-synced folder risks sync locks during writes (speculative; files currently show only the 'A' attribute, none cloud-only).
findings.evidence: mlflow.db experiments table: artifact_location 'file:///C:/Users/HP/OneDrive/Desktop/tata/artifacts/mlruns'; runs.artifact_uri all begin with that absolute prefix; artifacts/FD001/metrics.json 'mlflow_tracking_uri': 'sqlite:///C:/Users/HP/OneDrive/Desktop/tata/artifacts/mlflow.db'. `attrib` on artifacts/FD001/* shows 'A' only.
findings.recommendation: Demo from a non-synced local copy (e.g. C:\demo\tata) and build the frozen zip there so the absolute paths in mlflow.db match; or pass a relative `--default-artifact-root` when logging and document the required path in the runbook.

findings.title: Runbook promises 'calibration engines' in the Model & monitoring tab; the dashboard shows only the row count
findings.issue: Line 36 lists 'conformal calibration (alpha, qhat, calibration engines)'. dashboard.py line 105 renders alpha, qhat, n_calibration_rows, truncations_per_engine and assumption; the calibration_units list in conformal.json is never shown.
findings.evidence: dashboard.py line 105: `st.json({k: b.conformal.get(k) for k in ['alpha','qhat','n_calibration_rows','truncations_per_engine','assumption']})`; artifacts/FD001/conformal.json has 'calibration_units' (30 ids) and 'n_calibration_rows': 150.
findings.recommendation: Either add `len(calibration_units)`/the list to the st.json call or change the runbook wording to 'calibration rows'.

reviews.summary: I read README.md, the Round 1 slide (content plan and rendered PNG), the Round 2 deck plan, DEMO_SCRIPT, EXPERIMENT_RESULTS, KNOWN_LIMITATIONS, FAILURE_ANALYSIS, INNOVATION_HYPOTHESES, DECISION_LOG and CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX, then opened every summary.json and metrics.json they cite and the code paths behind the "zero false alarms", "deterministic / no LLM", "never look ahead", "tamper detected" and "retrain triggered by drift" claims. The worst problem is that the headline E3 result ("98–100% detection with zero false alarms; silent-wrong-order rate driven to zero") is largely true by construction: false alarms are change-relative to a clean run whose per-engine inputs are byte-identical, the drift-escalation reason is excluded from the false-alarm count, and the fleet drift alarm fired in all 20 scenarios so the full agent escalates every HIGH/CRITICAL engine; the definition was adopted (D19) after an absolute definition gave 52%, and none of the README, deck or demo script says any of this. The entry is unusually honest about H1/H2 and FD004 coverage, but H4's pre-registered failure is replaced on the deck by an unlabelled post-hoc run, several quoted numbers (elapsed 33–46 s, escalation 65–100%, "2–19% → zero") contradict the stored artefacts, the FD004 champion fails the system's own gate, and the slide presents an unwired drift→retrain trigger as built; overall verdict: not disqualifying, but a careful ML reviewer would discount the stress-test and MLOps claims until they are re-worded.

findings.title: "Zero false alarms" is zero by construction, and the redefinition that made it so is undisclosed
findings.issue: README ("catch missing values, noise and regime shifts on 98–100% of corrupted engines with zero false alarms"), deck slide 8 ("0 false alarms"), DEMO_SCRIPT Beat 5 ("with zero false alarms") and EXPERIMENT_RESULTS E3 present 0.0 false alarms as a measured result. In experiments/e3_stress.py the false-alarm rate is `newly(u, full, base_full)` over clean engines, where `newly` is change-relative to a clean run of the same engines; `process()` recomputes everything from fixed training-fit artefacts per unit, so a clean engine's quality flag, anomaly flag and decision cannot change. The one fleet-level input that does change (the drift alarm, passed to `decide(..., drift_alarm=rep_fleet_tail.alarm)`) adds the `drift_active` escalation (agent.py:98), but `newly` only checks ("data_quality", "conflicting_evidence"), contrary to its own docstring which lists "drift". So clean HIGH/CRITICAL engines newly escalated for drift are not counted as false alarms. DECISION_LOG D19 records that the change-relative definition was adopted after the absolute definition gave 52% false alarms (FAILURE_ANALYSIS §1 row 5). No submission document says the metric is change-relative or that the absolute rate was 52%.
findings.evidence: e3_stress.py:5-10 docstring: "Everything is CHANGE-RELATIVE to the clean run of the same engines... false alarm(u) = the same signals on CLEAN engines (which, being unchanged, can only come from the quality monitor or a fleet-level drift alarm)"; e3_stress.py:120 `esc_new = any(... for r in ("data_quality", "conflicting_evidence"))`; agent.py:97-98 `if obs.drift_flag and severity in ("HIGH","CRITICAL"): reasons.append("drift_active")`; summary.json: `fleet_drift_alarm_mixed_tail` is true in all 20 rows; DECISION_LOG D19: "counting them as false alarms (52%) was wrong".
findings.recommendation: State in README, deck slide 8 and demo script that detection and false alarms are change-relative to a clean run and that the absolute false-alarm rate on clean late-life engines was 52%; either include `drift_active` in `newly()` and re-report, or report separately the share of clean engines escalated for drift in each scenario. Drop the phrase "zero false alarms" unless that number survives.

findings.title: "Silent-wrong-order rate driven to zero" is produced by the fleet drift alarm escalating every HIGH/CRITICAL engine, not by per-engine detection
findings.issue: Deck slide 8 ("silent-wrong-order rate 0 (full agent) vs 2–19% (point-threshold agent)"), README line 16 and DEMO_SCRIPT Beat 5 ("went from 2–19% to zero") present this as the quality monitors catching bad inputs. In E3 the full agent receives `drift_alarm=rep_fleet_tail.alarm`, which was True in all 20 scenarios, and agent.py escalates every HIGH/CRITICAL decision when drift is active; `silent_wrong` counts only non-escalated HIGH/CRITICAL orders, so it is structurally 0 for the full agent whenever the fleet alarm fires. The naive agent is run with `drift_alarm=False`. The bias rows make this visible: per-engine detection is 4–20% on FD001/FD003 yet silent-wrong-order is still 0. Also, the naive rate is 0.000 in 3 of 20 rows (FD001 regime_shift, FD003 missing20, FD003 regime_shift), so "2–19% → zero" overstates the baseline, and denominators are 50 engines on FD001/FD003 (0.04 = 2 engines).
findings.evidence: e3_stress.py:116-117 `full = decide(last1, uq1, thr, drift_alarm=rep_fleet_tail.alarm, use_quality=True)` / `naive = decide(..., drift_alarm=False, use_quality=False)`; e3_stress.py:131 `silent_wrong` requires `not decs[u].escalate_to_human`; summary.json: all 20 `fleet_drift_alarm_mixed_tail` true; FD001 bias2s detection_rate 0.12, silent_wrong_order_full 0.0; rows with silent_wrong_order_naive == 0: FD001 regime_shift, FD003 missing20, FD003 regime_shift.
findings.recommendation: Say explicitly that the full agent's zero comes mostly from the fleet-level drift rule (escalate all HIGH/CRITICAL while a fleet alarm is active) and report the cost of that rule (share of clean HIGH/CRITICAL engines escalated). Replace "2–19%" with "0–19%" and give engine counts alongside rates.

findings.title: Demo script's "on corrupted inputs for 65–100%" escalation share contradicts e3_stress/summary.json
findings.issue: Beat 6 says the agent escalates "on corrupted inputs for 65–100%". The stored `escalation_share_full_corrupted` ranges from 0.24 to 1.0 across the 20 rows; even excluding both bias faults it is 0.66–1.0, and the script does not say bias is excluded.
findings.evidence: experiments/results/e3_stress/summary.json: FD003 bias2s 0.24, FD003 bias3s 0.26, FD001 bias3s 0.36, FD001 bias2s 0.38, FD004 bias2s 0.653, FD003 noise3s 0.66; others 0.74–1.0.
findings.recommendation: Change to "24–100% depending on the fault (66–100% for missing values, noise and regime shift; 24–38% for a single biased sensor on FD001/FD003)".

findings.title: H4's pre-registered failure is replaced on the deck and in the README by an unlabelled post-hoc run
findings.issue: Slide 2 promises "negative results are on slides 7 and 9", but slide 9 never says H4 was NOT SUPPORTED. It reports "more-data challenger promoted on FD002/FD003; label-corrupted challenger rejected on all four subsets" (numbers from the secondary run) and reframes the pre-registered corrupted-data scenario as "a harmless sensor offset is promoted". The pre-registered H4 required the gate to "visibly reject a challenger trained on corrupted data"; that challenger was PROMOTED on FD002–FD004 and the more-data challenger was falsely rejected on FD001 (4/8). The secondary run is labelled post hoc in D21 and EXPERIMENT_RESULTS but not on the deck. README line 16 lists E1, E2 and FD004 coverage as the negative results ("all reported, none hidden") and omits H4 entirely.
findings.evidence: e4_retrain_gate/summary.json conclusion: "4/8 scenario outcomes as expected ... Pre-registered criterion: NOT SUPPORTED"; table rows FD002/FD003/FD004 B_reject_corrupted_data decision PROMOTE, FD001 A_accept_more_data decision REJECT (`picp 0.800 < 0.85`); INNOVATION_HYPOTHESES H4: "visibly rejects a challenger trained on corrupted data"; DECISION_LOG D21: "adds a SECONDARY run, labelled post hoc"; README line 16 negative list omits H4.
findings.recommendation: On slide 9 add one line: "Pre-registered H4 NOT SUPPORTED (4/8): the +3σ offset challenger passed validation on 3/4 subsets; label-corruption scenario added post hoc (D21)." Add H4 to the README's negative-results sentence.

findings.title: "33–46 s per subset" contradicts the elapsed_s stored in artifacts/<subset>/metrics.json
findings.issue: Slide 3 and CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX C18 state "33–46 s per subset" with evidence "`elapsed_s` in metrics". The current metrics.json files (the artefact a judge would open) record 51.0 / 61.9 / 53.0 / 76.0 s; the 33–46 s figures come from the stage-1 log, which the stage-5 rerun superseded.
findings.evidence: artifacts/FD001..FD004/metrics.json `elapsed_s`: 51.0, 61.9, 53.0, 76.0; experiments/results/full_run_stage1_pipeline.log lines 18/26/34/42: "done in 33.2 s / 46.4 s / 34.6 s / 39.4 s".
findings.recommendation: Quote the range from the artefact that will be shipped ("33–76 s depending on run and machine load") or restate C18's evidence as the stage-1 log only.

findings.title: FD004 champion (PICP 0.82) fails the system's own promotion-gate floor and was never gated
findings.issue: The slide's side loop advertises "promotion gate (RMSE, coverage ≥ 0.85, late-order rate)" next to FD004 results, the README thesis says the system "retrains only through a promotion gate", and deck slide 9 repeats "PICP ≥ 0.85". The pipeline registers the initial model as `champion` unconditionally (no gate), and the FD004 champion's test coverage is 0.8226, below the 0.85 floor the gate would apply to any challenger. FAILURE_ANALYSIS §2.4 admits "the PICP gate threshold (0.85) would have flagged FD004" but README, slide and deck do not.
findings.evidence: src/sentinelloop/pipeline.py:160 `model_name=f"sentinelloop-{subset}", alias="champion"` with no `evaluate_gate` call (grep of pipeline.py/cli.py for "retrain|evaluate_gate" returns nothing); artifacts/FD004/metrics.json `picp_test_capped` 0.8225806; FAILURE_ANALYSIS line 22.
findings.recommendation: State on slide 5 / README that the initial champion is registered without the gate and that FD004's champion would not pass the gate's coverage floor as shipped; or gate the initial registration and report the outcome.

findings.title: Round 1 slide presents a drift-triggered retraining job as built; nothing in the package triggers retraining
findings.issue: The rendered slide shows "RETRAIN JOB triggered by a drift alarm or a new data file" and the italic line "accept AND reject paths are demonstrated; rejected challengers are logged with their reasons", and the Triage box says "drift alarm or new data starts retraining". In the package, `retrain.py` exposes only `evaluate_gate`; the CLI has doctor/data/baseline/run/audit/dashboard and no retrain command; pipeline.py only records `drift_alarm_test` and passes the flag to the agent. Retraining happens only inside experiments/e4_retrain_gate.py, whose drift scenario (C_drift_trigger) measures alarms and does not start any training.
findings.evidence: grep of src/sentinelloop for "retrain|evaluate_gate" outside retrain.py: only dashboard/viewdata display of retrain_log.json; cli.py:85-92 subparsers list; retrain.py public API: `class GateResult`, `def evaluate_gate`; e4_retrain_gate.py:119-140 drift scenario only counts alarms.
findings.recommendation: Re-word the slide box to "retraining job (scripted; gate evaluated on every challenger)" and the Triage bullet to "a drift alarm is logged and is the documented trigger for the retraining script", or wire a `retrain` CLI command that runs on an alarm before claiming the trigger.

findings.title: Batch imputer back-fills from future cycles; "never look ahead" and "stream equals batch (tested)" hold only on complete data
findings.issue: The slide says "Missing values: per-unit forward/backward fill", "Causal windows ... never look ahead" and "identical code in batch and stream mode (tested equal)"; deck slide 3 and C5 say "stream mode equals batch (tested)". `clean.impute` runs ffill then bfill per unit, so a missing value at cycle t is filled from t+1.. in batch mode, and E3's missing-20% stress test runs through this batch path. `CleanStream` keeps state "for forward-fill" only, and the single stream test contains no NaN case, so the equality claim is untested exactly where the two paths differ.
findings.evidence: clean.py:27-28 `out[cols] = out.groupby("unit")[cols].ffill()` then `.bfill()`; stream.py:3 "CleanStream keeps per-unit state for forward-fill and EMA"; tests/test_stream.py has one test (`test_incremental_features_match_batch_features`) and no occurrence of nan/missing; e3_stress.py:48 `imp = clean.impute(raw_test)`.
findings.recommendation: Either drop bfill (use ffill plus the quality flag) so batch is causal, or state on the slide that back-fill is batch-only and add a stream-vs-batch test with injected NaNs; re-run E3 missing20 if the imputer changes.

findings.title: "Tampering is detected" is only demonstrated for an edit that leaves the hash untouched; the chain has no secret or external anchor
findings.issue: README ("tampering is detected"), deck slide 9 ("tamper detected") and H6 present tamper detection without qualification. The E6 tamper flips one record's `severity` and rewrites the line without recomputing `hash`; audit.py uses plain SHA-256 with GENESIS = "0"*64 and no HMAC key, signature or external anchor, so anyone with write access can edit a record and re-hash the rest of the chain undetected. THREAT_MODEL_AND_FAILURE_MODES.md does not mention chain rewriting (grep for rewrite/anchor/hmac/tamper: no hits).
findings.evidence: e6_audit_check.py:21-23 `rec["severity"] = "NONE" if ... ; lines[...] = json.dumps(rec)`; audit.py:12 `GENESIS = "0" * 64`, :20 `hashlib.sha256(_canonical(rec)).hexdigest()`, no key material.
findings.recommendation: Qualify the claim: "an edit that does not re-hash the chain is detected; the chain is not protected against an insider who rewrites it (no external anchor)" and add that line to the threat model and KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.

findings.title: README coverage column shows capped-truth coverage only, while the RMSE column shows both; raw coverage is 0.56 on FD004
findings.issue: The results table labels the column "90% interval coverage" and the RMSE column "capped / raw". The coverage numbers (0.94/0.90/0.91/0.82) are `picp_test_capped`; `picp_test_raw` is 0.87/0.68/0.80/0.56 and appears nowhere in README, deck or demo script (FAILURE_ANALYSIS mentions only FD002's 0.68). A judge reading the raw RMSE of 27 will ask about raw coverage.
findings.evidence: artifacts metrics.json `picp_test_raw`: FD001 0.87, FD002 0.6757, FD003 0.80, FD004 0.5565; CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX C4 says "(capped truth)" but README/deck slide 5 do not.
findings.recommendation: Label the column "coverage vs capped truth" and add the raw-truth coverage (or a footnote that the interval targets capped RUL and under-covers raw truth beyond the cap).

findings.title: H1 spun as "never late" when the point policy is also never late on 3/4 subsets
findings.issue: Slide 7 and DEMO_SCRIPT Beat 5 say "at the generic threshold the lower-bound policy is never late but discards 11–17 more cycles". At T=25 the point policy also has late rate 0.000 on FD001–FD003 (E1 calls the test "uninformative" there); "never late" is not a distinguishing property. Neither the deck nor the script states that H1's pre-registered criterion was NOT SUPPORTED, only that it is "not a free lunch".
findings.evidence: EXPERIMENT_RESULTS E1 table: A point ≤ 25 late 0.000/0.000/0.000/0.006 vs C 0.000 on all; e1_policy_replay/summary.json conclusion "criterion (>=3/4 on both): NOT SUPPORTED".
findings.recommendation: Write "at T=25 neither policy is late on FD001–FD003; the lower-bound policy removes FD004's one late order and discards 11–18 more cycles; pre-registered H1 NOT SUPPORTED".

findings.title: "Tests were written before the code" is unverifiable (no git history) yet marked VERIFIED
findings.issue: The slide footer ("pytest (tests written before the code)"), README layout and deck slide 3 ("103 tests written before the code") make a process claim. The project is not a git repository, so no commit order exists; C19 cites `tests/` and a test log, which prove the tests exist and pass (103 collected), not when they were written. The matrix promises "every claim with the artefact that proves it".
findings.evidence: Environment: "Is a git repository: false"; pytest --collect-only sums to 103 tests; C19 evidence column: "`tests/`, `experiments/results/test_full_phase5.log`".
findings.recommendation: Downgrade C19 to "process claim, not independently verifiable" and soften the slide/deck wording to "103 tests (unit + integration)" unless a repository history can be published.

findings.title: Round 1 slide wording presents Round 2 evidence as already shown and misdescribes where thresholds are set
findings.issue: Slide text: "thresholds are tuned on validation engines, never on test; stress-test detection and false-alarm rates are reported" and "(the reject case is shown too)". The slide reports no stress-test rates and shows no reject case. The anomaly threshold is the 99th percentile of healthy-phase scores on training engines, not validation engines; the severity thresholds 10/25/50 are a priori (FAILURE_ANALYSIS §2.6 "chosen a priori"). Also round1_slide_content.md line 23 still says "A deep challenger is logged in MLflow for comparison" although no deep model exists in src (the rendered slide was changed to "RF and naive baselines are logged").
findings.evidence: anomaly.py:52 `det.threshold = float(np.percentile(det.score(train_f.loc[healthy]), threshold_pct))`; make_round1_slide.py:156-160; grep of src/sentinelloop for lstm/keras/torch: no model code; round1_slide_content.md:23.
findings.recommendation: Change to "anomaly threshold set on the healthy phase of training engines; severity thresholds fixed a priori, tuned in Round 2"; replace "are reported"/"is shown too" with "will be reported in Round 2"; delete the deep-challenger sentence from the content plan.

findings.title: "227 work orders" double-counts stream-replay orders for engines already ordered in batch; README table gives 218
findings.issue: E6, C9 and deck slide 6 say 227 orders; the README table lists 37/89/22/70 (= 218, `n_work_orders_batch`). The 9 extra are `n_work_orders_stream` (2/3/2/2) created when the first N test engines are replayed cycle by cycle, i.e. second orders for engines that already have batch orders.

reviews.summary: I read the Case Study 1 PDF (pdftotext), PROBLEM_SELECTION, SCORING_AND_RISKS, both submission content files, the rendered Round 1 slide, DEMO_SCRIPT, DEMO_RUNBOOK, EXPERIMENT_RESULTS, KNOWN_LIMITATIONS, README, the claim matrix, and verified every quoted number against artifacts/FD00x/metrics.json, retrain_log.json, the audit logs and experiments/results/e0-e7 summaries. The worst problem is persuasion order: the thesis sentence on the Round 1 slide, Round 2 slide 1 and the README leads with "work orders from the RUL lower bound" and "escalates only untrustworthy cases", which are precisely the two mechanisms the entry's own E1/E2 results do not support (lower bound = +70% discarded life at the default threshold, no late-rate gain on 3/4 subsets; clean-data escalations are 100% width-triggered and no more error-prone than acted-upon engines), while the genuinely strong measured results (silent-wrong-order 0 vs 0-19%, 0 false alarms, 3,409/0 audit re-derivation, label-corrupted challenger rejected 4/4) sit on slides 8-9; on top of that the primary demo subset FD001 has no PROMOTE row in its retrain log although the script says the gate promotes, the agent in the demo runs on thresholds (10/25/50) the team's own failure analysis says would over-maintain, and the deck's "33-46 s per subset" disagrees with the 51-76 s in the current metrics.json. Rubric mapping: Working pipeline 20 and Data engineering 15 and Dataset coverage 10 are well served; Demo & explanation 20 is honest but buries the wins and never translates late rate / discarded life into the PDF's "unplanned downtime / maintenance cost" vocabulary; MLOps 10 is adequate on paper but fragile in the demo; Agent behaviour 10 is undermined by untuned thresholds and the E2 null; Model performance 15 is the weakest line (14.4 vs published 11-13 and a public CPU LightGBM at 12.1, with no literature band on slide 5) - the verdict is a technically honest, well-evidenced entry that currently argues against itself in its first sentence and lacks a deploy-to-a-real-fleet story a Tata Elxsi engineering manager would expect.

findings.title: Thesis leads with the one mechanism the experiments did not support
findings.issue: Slide 1 (and the Round 1 title band, README line 3) opens with 'raises work orders from the RUL uncertainty lower bound'. The entry's own E1 shows this is not an improvement over a point threshold: same late rate (0.000 vs 0.000 on FD001-FD003) and 11-17 more cycles of life discarded per engine, i.e. 42.9 vs 25.2 cycles on FD001 = about 70% more serviceable life thrown away at the default threshold. A maintenance manager reading slide 1 is promised a benefit that slide 7 then retracts ('not a free lunch'). The measured strengths (E3 silent-wrong-order 0, 0 false alarms; E6 3,409 decisions re-derived with 0 mismatches; E4 label-corrupted challenger rejected 4/4) are on slides 8-9, after two negative-result slides. The one-minute 'why is this better than a point-RUL threshold' test fails.
findings.evidence: round2_deck_content.md line 7: 'raises work orders from the RUL uncertainty lower bound'. docs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md line 24: 'the interval policy's benefit is a lower late rate at a given tuned threshold, not less discarded life'. experiments/results/e1_policy_replay/summary.json FD001: A_point_T late 0.0 / discarded 25.17; C_lower_T late 0.0 / discarded 42.89. e3_table.csv: silent_wrong_order_full 0.0 on all 20 rows. e6 summary.json: n 3409, mismatches 0.
findings.recommendation: Re-order the thesis to lead with what was measured: 'never issues a confident wrong work order on corrupted inputs (0 vs up to 19% for a point-threshold agent), every order re-derivable from its audit record, bad retrains visibly rejected'. Present the lower bound as a tunable operating point on the late-rate/discarded-life frontier, not as the headline benefit. Move E3/E6/E4-B2 to slide 2's 'what to look for'.

findings.title: 'Escalates only untrustworthy cases to a human' is contradicted by the entry's own audit logs and E2
findings.issue: The README, the rendered Round 1 slide title band and Round 2 slide 1 all say the agent 'escalates only untrustworthy cases'. On clean official test data every escalation is width-triggered (insufficient_evidence) plus a few conflicting_evidence; none is a data-quality or drift escalation (quality_flag_rate_test 0.0, drift_alarm_test false). E2 shows those escalated engines are no more error-prone than the acted-upon ones (FD001: 0.143 among escalated vs 0.175 acted-upon). So 7-15% of clean-data engines are sent to a human with no measured decision benefit; that is human workload without return, and the deck never states this cost in business terms (inspections per 100 machines).
findings.evidence: artifacts/audit/decisions_FD00x.jsonl (counted): FD001 31 escalations, all insufficient_evidence; FD002 96, all insufficient_evidence; FD003 11 insufficient_evidence + 6 conflicting_evidence; FD004 41 + 1. artifacts/FD00x/metrics.json escalation_share_test 0.15 / 0.093 / 0.11 / 0.073, quality_flag_rate_test 0.0, drift_alarm_test false. experiments/results/e2_abstention/summary.json: relative_reduction -0.019 / -0.108 / 0.0 / -0.011, conclusion 'NOT SUPPORTED'.
findings.recommendation: Reword to 'escalates when inputs fail quality or drift checks, or the interval is wider than its calibrated limit'. On slide 6 add the clean-data cost explicitly (e.g. 'FD001: 15 inspections per 100 engines on clean data, no measured error reduction; the width rule earns its keep only on corrupted inputs, E3'). Consider making the width rule off by default on clean fleets or raising max_width so escalation share on clean data is near zero.

findings.title: Primary demo subset FD001 has no PROMOTE row; the script says the gate promotes
findings.issue: The runbook produces demo artefacts for FD001 (FD004 optional) and step 3 points at the 'retraining log with the PROMOTE and REJECT rows'. The FD001 retrain log contains only REJECT decisions, including the scenario named A_accept_more_data (rejected twice: 'picp 0.800 < 0.85', 'picp 0.835 < 0.85'). DEMO_SCRIPT Beat 5 says 'A challenger trained on more data is promoted when it is no worse on validation' - false on the subset being shown. On FD002-FD004 the opposite embarrassment appears: rows labelled B_reject_corrupted_data show PROMOTE. A judge watching the dashboard on FD001 sees a gate that never accepts; on FD002 sees a scenario whose name announces 'reject' and whose outcome is 'PROMOTE'. Slide 9 also mixes sourcing (promoted on 'FD002/FD003' = secondary run) with C13 (promoted on 'FD002-FD004' = primary run).
findings.evidence: artifacts/FD001/retrain_log.json (loaded): 7 entries, decisions REJECT, REJECT, -, REJECT, REJECT, REJECT, -; no PROMOTE. artifacts/FD002/retrain_log.json: B_reject_corrupted_data -> PROMOTE (twice), B2_reject_label_corruption -> REJECT 'rmse 20.904 > 16.757'. docs/DEMO_SCRIPT.md line 22. src/sentinelloop/dashboard.py line 108-110 renders retrain_log as-is.
findings.recommendation: Make FD002 or FD003 the gate-demo subset (A PROMOTE and B2 REJECT in the same log) and say so in the runbook. Rename scenario labels in retrain_log.json to neutral names ('more_data', 'sensor_offset', 'label_error') so the label does not pre-announce an expectation the outcome contradicts; keep the expected/observed comparison in the E4 README, not in the log a judge sees live. Use one E4 run consistently on slide 9.

findings.title: Demo agent runs on thresholds the entry's own analysis says would over-maintain
findings.issue: All four subsets use t_critical 10 / t_high 25 / t_medium 50 on the lower bound (per-subset yaml files override only n_regimes). FAILURE_ANALYSIS states 'Deploying the generic values would over-maintain' and E1 reports tuned lower-bound thresholds of 5-8. Every one of the 227 work orders, the severity counts on slide 6 and the 'CRITICAL engine' shown in Beat 4 come from the rule the authors have rejected. For 'Agent behavior: the agent acts correctly and reliably on the model output' (10%) and 'Demo' (20%) judges see an agent acting on an operating point its builders call wrong, without the deck saying so on the slide where the orders are shown.
findings.evidence: configs/default.yaml lines 33-35: t_critical: 10, t_high: 25, t_medium: 50; configs/FD001.yaml and FD004.yaml contain only subset and clean.n_regimes. docs/FAILURE_ANALYSIS.md line 24: 'Deploying the generic values would over-maintain.' docs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md line 28: 'tuned lower-bound thresholds 5-8 give 1-5% late rates with 12-16 cycles discarded'. artifacts/FD001/metrics.json agent_thresholds t_high 25.0.
findings.recommendation: Either ship the E1-tuned thresholds per subset in configs/FD00x.yaml (agent.t_critical/t_high) and re-run so the demo orders match the recommended operating point, or add one line to slide 6: 'Operating point shown: conservative default (10/25/50, 0% late, 37-43 cycles discarded); tuned alternative 5-8 (1-5% late, 12-16 discarded) - the fleet manager chooses'. Do not let slide 7 be the first place the judge learns the demo thresholds are untuned.

findings.title: Deck quotes '33-46 s per subset' but the current metrics.json artefacts say 51-76 s
findings.issue: Slide 3 and claim C18 state the pipeline takes 33-46 s per subset. The deck's own rule (line 3) is that every number is copied from a stored artefact. The artefacts the pipeline writes (artifacts/FD00x/metrics.json, from the stage-5 re-run) record 51.0 / 61.9 / 53.0 / 76.0 s. The 33-46 s figures exist only in the earlier stage-1 log. A judge who opens metrics.json finds the deck's number wrong by up to 2x.
findings.evidence: artifacts/FD001..FD004/metrics.json elapsed_s: 51.0, 61.9, 53.0, 76.0. experiments/results/full_run_stage1_pipeline.log lines 18/26/34/42: 'done in 33.2 s', '46.4 s', '34.6 s', '39.4 s'. CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md C18: 'full run 33-46 s per subset'.
findings.recommendation: Quote the artefact that ships: 'under 80 s per subset on a CPU laptop (51-76 s in the stored run; 33-46 s on an idle machine, stage-1 log)'. Update C18 and slide 3 together.

findings.title: Late rate and discarded life are never translated into the PDF's business terms; the cost-sensitive sweep is left out of the deck
findings.issue: Slide 7 and Beat 5 speak of 'late rate' and 'discards 11-17 more cycles per engine'. The PDF defines the problem as 'unplanned downtime and higher maintenance cost'. Nowhere does the deck say late order = breakdown in service, discarded life = a part replaced while it still had N cycles, nor the relative size (+70% life discarded at the default threshold). The only analysis a manager could act on - policy D, where the chosen threshold moves from 8-12 to 12-18 cycles as the assumed failure cost rises from 25 to 500 cycles of life - is in EXPERIMENT_RESULTS but absent from the deck plan, which mentions cost ratios only as a limitation on slide 10.
findings.evidence: PDF page 1 (pdftotext): 'leading to unplanned downtime and higher maintenance cost'. grep for downtime|cost|breakdown|unplanned in round2_deck_content.md and round1_slide_content.md: only slide 10 'no real cost claim'. docs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md line 25: 'thresholds move from 8-12 (cheap failures) to 12-18 cycles (expensive failures)'. e1 summary.json FD001 D_cost_25 threshold 8.0, D_cost_500 threshold 12.0; FD004 D_cost_25 12.0, D_cost_500 18.0.
findings.recommendation: On slide 7 add a two-line glossary ('late order = unplanned breakdown; discarded life = serviceable life thrown away') and a small policy-D panel titled 'how a fleet manager sets the threshold from the breakdown-to-early-replacement cost ratio' (labelled as assumptions, no savings claimed). State the relative number (+70%) next to the absolute one.

findings.title: No 'what it would take to deploy' story for an engineering-services judge

findings.recommendation: Retitle slide 10 'Path to a real fleet' with four steps each anchored to an existing artefact: (1) work_orders.json schema -> CMMS/ERP adapter (SAP PM / Maximo fields named); (2) telemetry adapter: C-MAPSS cycle = trip/engine-hour, per-asset-class regime clustering already config-driven; (3) threshold tuning per fleet with the E1 replay on the fleet's own run-to-failure history, with the policy-D cost ratio as the input; (4) relative coverage floor (KNOWN_LIMITATIONS 21) and staffing from escalation share. findings.title: Model performance (15%) is the weakest rubric line and slide 5 hides the comparison that matters

reviews.summary: I read docs/OFFICIAL_REQUIREMENTS.md, docs/SCORING_AND_RISKS.md, PROJECT_STATUS.md, submission/make_round1_slide.py, round1_slide_content.md, round2_deck_content.md, CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md and docs/DEMO_RUNBOOK.md, viewed round1_slide.png at full size and at 320/640 px thumbnails, inspected round1_slide.pdf in binary (1 page, 70,482 bytes, 16:9, Type 3 fonts, no Title metadata), extracted the Round 1 wording from the official Case Study 1 PDF, and cross-checked every number on the slide against experiments/results/e0_baseline/*_metrics.json. The worst problems are logistical rather than technical: with 5 days to the registration deadline and 6 to the Round 1 deadline, registration, upload mechanics, team leader and git remote are all still OPEN with no evidence of completion; the shipped PDF carries the placeholder "(college to be filled)"; and the entry committed to a single slide on the strength of the Unstop listing while the official PDF says "Round 1 submission are design and Architecture slides deck", which produced an ~800-word slide set in 6.0–6.7 pt type that is illegible at thumbnail scale and unreadable in 60 seconds. findings.title: No labelled 'Problem understanding' section (15% of Round 1) and no explicit rubric map on the slide
findings.issue: The slide's visible headers are 'Data engineering approach', 'Dataset coverage', 'Triage Agent logic (deterministic) and MLOps' and 'ML approach & reasoning'.
