verdicts.reasoning:
Every number in the finding reproduces exactly, but the headline claim ("contradicted by the entry's own audit logs and E2") does not hold, and everything the finding says is missing is already disclosed in the entry's own README, deck plan, claim matrix and docs.

(1) Not a contradiction. The entry defines "untrustworthy" in src/sentinelloop/agent.py lines 4-5 as "interval too wide, input quality bad, drift active while a serious order is due, or conflicting signals", and both slides print that rule table ("interval wider than calibrated limit ... ESCALATE"). The audit logs show the agent escalating exactly those cases (all clean-data escalations are R_ESC_WIDTH / R_ESC_CONFLICT), so the logs confirm the sentence rather than contradict it. The finding's real point is semantic: E2 shows a wide interval does not predict decision error, so "untrustworthy" is a design label, not an empirically backed one.

(2) Already disclosed, in the same documents the finding cites. README line 16 (13 lines below the thesis): "width-based abstention alone did not reduce decision errors (E2)". README table column "escalated to a human": 15% / 9% / 11% / 7%, i.e. the inspections-per-100-engines figure the finding says is never stated. Round 2 deck slide 6 prints escalation share 0.15/0.09/0.11/0.07; slide 7 prints "E2: width-based abstention does not concentrate errors (H2 rejected)"; slide 2 promises the negative results on slides 7 and 9. submission/CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md C11: "H2 NOT SUPPORTED, 0/4; escalation share on clean data 7-20%". docs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md line 38: "abstention on interval width alone is not a decision-quality mechanism on clean C-MAPSS data; its value is as an input-trust mechanism (E3). The deck does not claim H2." docs/FAILURE_ANALYSIS.md line 23: "Escalation share is model-dependent (7-20%) ... a fleet must set the acceptable share explicitly." docs/DECISION_LOG.md D16 explains the width limit is the 75th percentile of serious calibration widths, so a non-zero clean-data share is by construction and documented.

(3) The "off by default / raise max_width" recommendation is a design preference, not a defect; D16 records why a fixed limit was rejected and configs/default.yaml exposes max_width as a tunable.

What survives is a wording nit: the thesis line uses "untrustworthy" where "low-confidence or failed-check" would be more defensible, and slide 6 does not put the share and the E2 null result in one sentence. A judge who reads slides 6 and 7 together gets both facts; this is not something a judge would penalise beyond a minor presentation point. Severity high is not justified; low at most.

The 'hidden cost' claim is also wrong: the escalation shares 0.15/0.09/0.11/0.07 ARE inspections per 100 engines on clean test data (escalation_share_test = escalated units / n_test_units, FD001 15/100) and they are printed on README line 9-14 as a column titled 'escalated to a human', on Round 2 slide 6, and in CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX C11 ('escalation share on clean data 7-20%'). A judge scoring Agent behavior (10%) or Demo & explanation (20%) sees a thesis, a rule table that defines escalation including width, a share per subset, and a slide saying H2 was rejected; that is a coherent honest story and a reasonable Q&A, not a penalty. The recommendation adds nothing substantive: the proposed rewording restates the slide's own rule table; '15 inspections per 100 engines' is 0.15 already on slide 6; turning the width rule off or raising max_width contradicts the documented D16 decision, would require re-running E1-E3, and the project already states the share must be set per fleet. verdicts.reasoning: Every factual claim reproduces: configs/default.yaml lines 33-35 set t_critical 10 / t_high 25 / t_medium 50; all four per-subset yamls (FD001-FD004) override only `subset` and `clean.n_regimes`; all four artifacts/FD00x/metrics.json and agent_thresholds.json carry t_high 25.0; src/sentinelloop/agent.py lines 82-84 assign severity from `obs.rul_lower <= t_critical / t_high`, so the agent does act on the lower bound at these values; work_orders.json totals 39+92+24+72 = 227; FAILURE_ANALYSIS.md line 24 reads verbatim "Deploying the generic values would over-maintain"; EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md line 28 reads "tuned lower-bound thresholds 5-8 give 1-5% late rates with 12-16 cycles discarded"; slide 6 in submission/round2_deck_content.md shows the 10/25/50 rule table, severity counts and "227 orders" with no untuned/generic caveat; DEMO_SCRIPT Beat 4 picks "a CRITICAL engine". So the finding is literally true. The HIGH severity is not supported, however. (1) The caveat is on the immediately following slide 7 ("at the generic threshold ... tuned thresholds 5-8 ... a conservative operating point the operator chooses"), on slide 10 ("thresholds must be tuned per fleet"), spoken in Beat 5 and Beat 7, and in two docs; the finding itself concedes slide 7 discloses it, so the complaint is slide ordering within a deck explicitly marked DRAFT pending red-team review. (2) The authors never call the operating point "wrong" or "rejected"; they call it "chosen a priori" and "conservative" with 0% late rate, which is the safe failure mode and a defensible demo default (the tuned 5-8 would show 1-5% of engines failing before the order). (3) The dashboard does not render agent thresholds at all (dashboard.py only plots the anomaly threshold), so nothing on screen in Beat 4 misleads. Residual real issue the reviewer missed: KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md item 14 ("Thresholds are tuned on a tuning split of training engines") and the already-submitted Round 1 slide (make_round1_slide.py line 156: "thresholds are tuned on validation engines, never on test") both contradict FAILURE_ANALYSIS item 6 ("chosen a priori") and the shipped config; a judge who reads Round 1 and then the config could catch that. That wording fix, plus the one-line caveat on slide 6, is cheap and worth doing, but the exposure is low, not high.

verdicts.reasoning: The finding reproduces literally. experiments/results/e0_baseline/FD004_metrics.json has hgbr_rmse_raw = 27.048590629322145, which the slide script's `:.1f` formatting (submission/make_round1_slide.py line 119) prints as "27.0", and the rendered submission/round1_slide.png bottom-left reads "FD001 14.4 / 15.5 · FD002 14.9 / 27.1 · FD003 13.9 / 15.5 · FD004 15.4 / 27.0". CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md line 7 (C1) says "FD004 15.4/27.1" and round1_slide_content.md line 37 says "FD004 15.4 / 27.1"; round2_deck_content.md line 11, README.md, docs/REPRODUCIBILITY.md, docs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md and PROJECT_STATUS.md all say 27.05. The origin is a double-rounding slip: run.log line 4 prints "raw 27.05" at two decimals and someone rounded that half-up to 27.1, whereas the true value 27.0486 rounds to 27.0. All other C1 numbers (FD001 14.4/15.5, FD002 14.9/27.1, FD003 13.9/15.5) match the JSONs at one decimal. Nothing in the repo discloses the discrepancy. However, "high" is overstated: the artefact judges actually see (the slide PDF/PNG, generated from the JSONs) carries the correct 27.0; the wrong digit is confined to two planning/evidence documents and is a 0.05 rounding artefact, not a wrong result or an inflated claim. A judge cross-checking the matrix against the slide would notice a one-digit mismatch in a document that promises exact agreement, so it is worth the one-character fix, but it would not plausibly cost marks. Severity: low.

verdicts.reasoning: The finding is literally true and is not disclosed anywhere, so it is not refuted; but "high" is inflated by roughly two levels. What a judge actually sees is correct: the Round 1 PDF/PNG are generated straight from the JSON by make_round1_slide.py line 119 (`:.1f`), and f"{27.048590629322145:.1f}" is "27.0", which is what the rendered slide shows. That makes it worth the one-character fix in two files, and the recommendation (print 27.0, or 2 dp everywhere, plus a re-render check) is sensible and cheap, since no existing check compares the matrix to the JSONs (tests/test_baseline_smoke.py only asserts key presence and sanity bounds). critic.dimension: COMPLETENESS CRITIC (gaps missed by the nine prior reviewers: untested paths, artefact-vs-claim checks nobody ran, config/doc drift, registry state, audit threat model, dashboard)
critic.summary: I opened the Case Study 1 PDF, every test file, the agent/audit/pipeline/stream/drift/retrain/dashboard modules, the experiment scripts, all per-subset artefacts, both SQLite databases (read-only) and the stored experiment summaries, ran the fast test suite (97 passed, 6 deselected) and cross-checked stored artefacts against the claims that cite them. The worst problems: the "decision-metric" promotion gate that the entry presents as its differentiator has a late-rate branch that is identically 0.0 in all 20 stored gate evaluations (it replays at threshold 25 where the entry's own E1 says nobody is late); the MLflow registry's live `champion` alias for the FD002–FD004 gated models points to the challenger trained on deliberately corrupted sensors; and the "stream mode equals batch (tested)" claim is contradicted by the stored artefacts (40–49% of stream rows carry different predictions from the batch run, with anomaly-flag mismatches on FD003) because CleanStream and the end-to-end stream path are untested. Verdict: the entry's evidence is broad but several VERIFIED claims rest on paths that were never exercised (gate late-rate branch, stream path, audit truncation, work-order lifecycle), the registry state would embarrass a live MLflow demo, and the design/threat-model documents still describe eight mechanisms that do not exist in the code.

findings.title: The gate's late-rate check (the entry's claimed differentiator) is inert: 0.0 in all 20 stored evaluations
findings.issue: INNOVATION_HYPOTHESES.md:9 lists 'a promotion gate that uses a maintenance-decision metric' as the thing 'not found anywhere', and deck slide 9 sells 'Gate (RMSE +2%, PICP >= 0.85, late rate +0.02)'. But validation_metrics() replays policy C at thr.t_high (25 cycles), the exact threshold at which the entry's own E1 and FAILURE_ANALYSIS say nobody is late. Consequently every PROMOTE/REJECT in both E4 runs came from RMSE or PICP; the decision-safety branch never contributed and is only exercised by synthetic numbers in tests/test_gate.py:22.
findings.evidence: artifacts/FD001..FD004/retrain_log.json: all 20 scenario rows (primary A/B x4, secondary A/B/B2 x4) carry "champion_late_rate": 0.0 and "challenger_late_rate": 0.0, including B2 (labels +40 cycles optimistic, RMSE 19.8-20.9) whose reasons are only 'rmse ... ; picp ...'. e4_retrain_gate.py:49 `policy.Policy("C", "lower", thr.t_high)`; docs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md:21 'At the fixed 25-cycle threshold neither policy is late on FD001-FD003 (late rate 0.000 for both)'; FAILURE_ANALYSIS.md:19 'nobody is late at 25'.
findings.recommendation: Evaluate the late-rate gate at the tuned threshold (5-8 per E1) or at the frontier target, report the late rates it produces, and either show a case where it fires or stop presenting the gate as decision-metric-based.

findings.title: MLflow registry's live `champion` alias for FD002/FD003/FD004 gated models is the corrupted-data challenger; scenario B is gated against a stale champion
findings.issue: Scenario B ('+3 sigma sensor offset', expected REJECT) was PROMOTED on FD002-FD004 in both runs, and tr.promote() moved the `champion` alias to it; the secondary run was last, so the registry now says the champion of sentinelloop-FD00x-gated is the model trained on deliberately corrupted sensors. DEMO_RUNBOOK.md:40 tells the presenter to open the MLflow UI and show 'champion, accepted challenger, rejected challenger'. Separately, `cm` (champion metrics) is computed once at line 72, so after A is promoted scenario B is still compared with the original champion while the alias already points at A; the retrain_log's 'champion_rmse' is therefore not the registry champion. The gated registry (`sentinelloop-<subset>-gated`) is also a different registered model from the pipeline's `sentinelloop-<subset>`, so no promotion ever reaches the agent.
findings.evidence: artifacts/mlflow.db (read-only query): registered_model_aliases ('champion', 6, 'sentinelloop-FD002-gated'), ('champion', 6, 'sentinelloop-FD003-gated'), ('champion', 6, 'sentinelloop-FD004-gated'); model_versions v6 -> runs 88b0fc31.. / dc98cb11.. / 5860f35e.. whose mlflow.runName tags are 'FD002-B_reject_corrupted_data', 'FD003-B_reject_corrupted_data', 'FD004-B_reject_corrupted_data'. retrain_log.json FD002 secondary rows A and B both list champion_rmse 16.4286 although A was promoted (champion_alias_version 5) before B was gated.
findings.recommendation: Reset the gated registry to a clean champion before the demo, re-read the current champion's metrics before each gate evaluation, and either wire the gated champion into the pipeline model name or state in the deck that retraining is a side experiment that never feeds the agent.

findings.title: 'Stream mode equals batch (tested)' is contradicted by the stored artefacts: 40-49% of stream rows carry different predictions, with anomaly-flag mismatches on FD003
findings.issue: C5 (VERIFIED), deck slide 3, README.md:35 ('tested equal to batch') and PROJECT_STATUS.md:35 claim stream equals batch. The only test (tests/test_stream.py:8) feeds already-cleaned batch rows into FeatureStream and checks features to 1e-9; CleanStream (stream.py:17) and the end-to-end stream path are referenced by no test. The pipeline's own stream artefacts disagree with the batch predictions for the same engine-cycles.
findings.evidence: Merged artifacts/<subset>/decisions_stream.csv with predictions_test_all_cycles.csv on (unit, cycle): FD001 166/410 rows differ (max |dpoint| 1.64, |dlower| 0.32); FD002 max 2.08/0.42; FD003 393/797 rows differ (max |dpoint| 2.62, |dlower| 2.11, |dupper| 3.27) and 3 rows (unit 3 cycles 113/141, unit 1 cycle 196) have anomaly_flag True in stream vs False in batch; FD004 max 0.72/0.53. Re-running CleanStream+FeatureStream on FD001 unit 1 reproduces the stored stream numbers (diff 1e-14), gives features identical to batch within 1e-9, yet CQR predictions differ by up to 0.08: the tree model amplifies sub-1e-9 rolling differences (mechanism beyond that: unverified).
findings.recommendation: Add an end-to-end test that runs the real stream path (CleanStream -> FeatureStream -> cqr.predict -> triage) against the batch predictions on real data for all four subsets, fix or bound the discrepancy, and reword the claim to what is actually tested.

findings.title: Stream path is weaker than batch and non-causal: it reuses the whole-test-set drift alarm, has no window quality monitor, and records no escalation reasons
findings.issue: Every stream decision receives `drift_report.alarm` computed at line 120 on early-life rows of the ENTIRE test set (look-ahead for a 'cycle-by-cycle replay'); observation_from_row is called without quality_flag/imputed window stats, so in stream mode R_ESC_QUALITY can only fire on a single row with >10% of sensors imputed and the out-of-range/critical-setting rules never apply; decisions_stream.csv (line 219) stores no `reasons`, so the dashboard's stream table cannot say why a row escalated. E3 (e3_stress.py:47-63) corrupts data through the batch functions only, so R1 'stream VERIFIED' and R2's E3 evidence never cover missing values or regime shifts in stream mode.
findings.evidence: pipeline.py:216 `agent.triage(observation_from_row(srow, subset, run_id, drift_report.alarm, n_sensors), thr)`; pipeline.py:48 default `quality_flag: bool = False`; decisions_stream.csv columns: unit, cycle, point, lower, upper, anomaly_score, anomaly_flag, n_imputed, severity, action, escalate, order_event (no reasons). e3_stress.py:48 `imp = clean.impute(raw_test)` (batch).
findings.recommendation: Compute the drift flag from the stream's own trailing window, apply window_quality incrementally in stream mode, store reasons in decisions_stream.csv, and run at least the missing-20% fault through the stream path.

findings.title: Agent outcomes against ground truth on the official test set are never reported; computed numbers show misses on the side the agent acts on
findings.issue: Slide 6 ('Agent behavior 10') presents only severity counts and escalation share. No document gives severity-vs-true-RUL on the test engines. Computing it from decisions_test.csv: on FD004 the lower bound (the agent's decision variable) is ABOVE the true capped RUL for 42/248 engines (17%; FD002 27/259), 2 of 14 engines with true RUL <= 10 are not CRITICAL and 3 engines with true RUL 22-25 are only MEDIUM; on FD003, 9 of 11 CRITICAL engines (true RUL 6-18) are escalated to INSPECTION for width instead of STOP_AND_REPAIR; FD001 has one confident HIGH order on an engine with true RUL 85. The PDF rubric line is 'The agent acts correctly and reliably on the model output'.
findings.evidence: artifacts/FD004/decisions_test.csv: (rul_true_capped < rul_lower).sum() = 42; rows with rul_true_capped <= 10 and severity != CRITICAL = 2; units 1, 77, 187 MEDIUM with true 22/25/24. artifacts/FD003/decisions_test.csv: escalated-by-severity {CRITICAL: 9, HIGH: 2}, reasons all 'insufficient_evidence'. artifacts/FD001/decisions_test.csv: 1 non-escalated HIGH/CRITICAL with true RUL > 50.
findings.recommendation: Add a severity-vs-truth table (and lower-bound exceedance rate) per subset to the results and the deck, and explain or fix the FD003 behaviour where most CRITICAL engines are routed to inspection.

findings.title: Audit log is not append-only and truncation is undetectable; E6 tests only an in-place edit
findings.issue: pipeline.run deletes the per-subset audit log on every run ('a re-run of a subset starts its log afresh') and write_sqlite DELETEs all decisions for the subset (lines 30-31), so the trail of earlier runs is destroyed by the pipeline itself although audit.py:1 and SYSTEM_DESIGN.md:59 call it 'append-only'. verify_chain (audit.py:55-61) accepts any prefix: deleting trailing records passes, and AuditLog.__init__ (lines 29-34) resumes from the last surviving hash so delete-then-append is also invisible. replay_check (audit.py:88-89) compares severity/action/escalate/rules only, not escalation_reasons or interval_width. E6 (e6_audit_check.py:21-24) tampers one middle record's severity and nothing else.
findings.evidence: pipeline.py:172-174 `audit_path = ...; if audit_path.exists(): audit_path.unlink()`; audit.py:55-61 loop returns True for any valid prefix; e6_audit_check.py:22 `rec["severity"] = "NONE" ...` is the only tamper scenario; experiments/results/e6_audit_check/summary.json 'tampered' has one entry per log.
findings.recommendation: Keep a record count / terminal hash in a separate anchor (or in MLflow), rotate rather than unlink logs on re-run, test truncation and re-append in E6, and compare the full decision record in replay_check.

findings.title: Threat-model, design and decision-log 'controls' describe eight mechanisms that do not exist in the code (beyond the test_leakage and citation gaps already reported)
findings.issue: B2 says a wide interval gives 'WATCH + escalate ... never NONE' (agent.py:95-96 keeps MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL and only escalates); B3 'downgrades require k consecutive cycles' (no hysteresis anywhere; WorkOrderBook only upgrades and close() is never called); B4 and SYSTEM_DESIGN.md:59 `audit.explain()` (no such function); C3 'Dashboard reads with read-only connections' (it reads JSON/CSV files); C4 `python -m sentinelloop data --verify` (cli.py:86 has only --download/--subset); C6 '`run` uses cached artefacts unless `--force`' (cli.py:89-90 has no such flag; run always retrains); D1 'Dockerfile' (none in the tree); A2 'experiment scripts assert no test ids in tuning' (grep: zero `assert` in experiments/*.py). SYSTEM_DESIGN.md:25,55 and DECISION_LOG D4 (status VERIFIED) say drift uses 'KS / PSI' via scipy; drift.py implements PSI only and imports no scipy.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'def explain|--verify|--force|Dockerfile|book.close' src experiments -> no matches; grep 'ks_2samp|kstest|scipy' src/sentinelloop/*.py -> only the import check in cli.py:13; agent.py:95 `if width > thr.max_width and severity in ("MEDIUM","HIGH","CRITICAL"): reasons.append("insufficient_evidence")`.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the control/check columns to name only mechanisms that exist, or implement the missing ones (hysteresis, explain(), --verify) before Round 2.

findings.title: SYSTEM_DESIGN config excerpt contradicts configs/default.yaml on five keys, and `drift.window` is dead configuration for the pipeline
findings.issue: The 'excerpt' shows ema_alpha 0.3 (actual 0.0), agent.max_width 60 (actual 'auto'), quality_max_imputed_frac 0.2 (actual 0.1, pre-registered in D15), anomaly.contamination: auto (key absent) and a `regimes:` map (actual per-subset files), and omits severe_psi_threshold/early_life_max_cycle. `drift.window: 500` is read only by E4 (e4_retrain_gate.py:116); pipeline.py:103-110 never reads it, so the production drift check has no configurable window (it uses all early-life test rows: n_rows 3034 on FD001). The agent dataclass default quality_max_imputed_frac is 0.20 (agent.py:24) and tests/test_agent.py:5 tests 0.2, not the shipped 0.1.
findings.evidence: configs/default.yaml:8 `ema_alpha: 0.0`, :36 `max_width: auto`, :37 `quality_max_imputed_frac: 0.10`, :45 `window: 500`; SYSTEM_DESIGN.md:79-86; grep for `"window"` in src/sentinelloop shows only features window usage; artifacts/FD001/drift_reference.json test_window n_rows 3034.
findings.recommendation: Replace the excerpt with the real file (or generate it), delete or wire `drift.window`, and align the dataclass default and the unit-test thresholds with the pre-registered 0.10.

findings.title: Test-suite blind spots: stream cleaning, pipeline helpers, CLI, dashboard, every experiment script, multi-regime paths and several agent branches are untested
findings.issue: No test references CleanStream, pipeline.window_quality/observation_from_row/write_sqlite, cli.py, dashboard.py or anything under experiments/ (the E1-E7 scripts that generate every headline number have zero tests, including common.severities_for_engine). Agent branches without tests: missing_sensors > 0 (agent.py:93), drift+quality together, WorkOrderBook.close (agent.py:142), and the case where a later escalated decision at equal severity leaves an open MAINTENANCE order's type/reasons untouched (agent.py:134-140). CleanStream, AnomalyDetector and fit_cqr are never tested with n_regimes > 1 (test_stream/test_width_calibration use n_regimes=1); the only real-data integration tests are FD001 (test_pipeline_smoke.py:203, test_baseline_smoke.py). Gate late-rate branch only via synthetic numbers (test_gate.py:22).
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'CleanStream|window_quality|observation_from_row|write_sqlite|\.close(|missing_sensors=' tests/ -> only Observation constructors with missing_sensors=0; grep -rln experiments tests/ -> none; `pytest -m 'not slow'` -> 97 passed, 6 deselected (so the 103 total is correct but the coverage above is absent).
findings.recommendation: Add real-data tests for the stream path on FD002/FD004, a window_quality test with injected NaNs, an agent combination test, and smoke tests of each experiment script on a 2-engine fixture.

findings.title: Stored retrain_log.json artefacts were not written by the shipped e4_retrain_gate.py (missing `checks` key)
findings.issue: Line 89 appends `"checks": g.checks` to every logbook row and line 140 writes those rows to artifacts/<subset>/retrain_log.json, yet none of the 24 stored rows contains a `checks` key. The code was therefore edited after the evidence run, and with no version control (D9) nobody can tie the stored gate evidence to a code state; REPRODUCIBILITY.md:63 says numbers are 'copied from the summary.json files written by these runs'.
findings.evidence: grep -c '"checks"' artifacts/*/retrain_log.json -> 0 for all four files; keys of every row: run, subset, scenario, expected, decision, as_expected, champion_rmse, challenger_rmse, champion_picp, challenger_picp, champion_late_rate, challenger_late_rate, reasons, mlflow_run_id, champion_alias_version, ts.
findings.recommendation: Re-run E4 with the shipped script (or restore the script that produced the artefacts) and initialise version control so artefacts carry a commit hash.

findings.title: The auto-generated work order carries no actionable content, is never closed, and the 'names the sensors' explainability is computed nowhere
findings.issue: The PDF requires the agent to 'automatically create a maintenance work order'. The record holds id/unit/type/severity/status/created_cycle/updated_cycle/reasons/model_version/n_decisions/mode: no RUL point or interval, no `action` (STOP_AND_REPAIR/SCHEDULE_MAINTENANCE exists only in the decision), no due-by cycle, no timestamp, no offending sensors. `status` is always OPEN because WorkOrderBook.close (agent.py:142) is never called. anomaly.top_deviations (anomaly.py:70, 'explainability for the dashboard and audit') is called by no module, so OFFICIAL_REQUIREMENTS.md:53 R4 'names the sensors' and SYSTEM_DESIGN.md:53 are unsupported by any artefact. KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md:9 promises 'a documented schema'; no schema document exists.
findings.evidence: artifacts/FD001/work_orders.json keys: ['created_cycle','id','mode','model_version','n_decisions','reasons','severity','status','type','unit','updated_cycle']; all 227 orders status OPEN; grep -rn top_deviations src experiments tests -> only the definition; grep -rin schema docs README submission -> only the KNOWN_LIMITATIONS sentence.
findings.recommendation: Put the RUL interval, action, due-by cycle, timestamp and top deviating sensors into the order record, implement close-on-maintenance in the replay, and write the schema in SYSTEM_DESIGN.

findings.title: No .gitignore while the slide promises a public repository: the NASA archive the docs say is 'not redistributed', the venv, pickles and absolute-path MLflow DB would all ship
findings.issue: REPRODUCIBILITY.md:12 and THREAT_MODEL E1 state the archive is not bundled and only a download script is provided; yet data/raw/ in the project tree holds pcoe_turbofan.zip (12.4 MB), CMAPSSData.zip, the NASA PDF and all 12 txt files (~45 MB), DEMO_RUNBOOK.md:10 says 'copy data/raw/ from the team share', and there is no .gitignore. A plain `git add .` (the slide footer promises a public repo; others flagged the missing remote) would redistribute the dataset and commit .venv, artifacts/*.pkl (KNOWN_LIMITATIONS 17 warns never to load untrusted pickles) and mlflow.db with absolute OneDrive paths.
findings.evidence: ls -la .gitignore -> 'No such file or directory'; ls data/raw -> CMAPSSData.zip, pcoe_turbofan.zip, Damage Propagation Modeling.pdf, train/test/RUL_FD001..4.txt; MIT LICENSE present at project root.
findings.recommendation: Add a .gitignore excluding data/raw, .venv, artifacts/*.pkl, *.db and mlruns before any push, and reconcile the licence/IP wording with the non-redistribution statement.

findings.title: Monitoring view and MLflow tracking omit the agent-level signals: no per-engine quality/drift columns, no registry versions in the dashboard, subset-agnostic Experiments tab, and MLflow never receives escalation/work-order/runtime metrics
findings.issue: R8 'basic monitoring view' and 'track experiments and model versions' (PDF MLOps layer): the sidebar prints only the pipeline run id from metrics.json; the dashboard never reads the registry, so model versions/aliases are invisible. fleet_table (viewdata.py:71) exposes no imputed_frac, quality_flag or drift_flag column, so the human sees 'INSPECT' without the input-quality evidence. The Experiments tab (dashboard.py:113-121) renders every summary regardless of the selected subset, and the retrain-log table mixes gate rows with C_drift_trigger rows of a different shape. In pipeline.py:156-157 the MLflow metrics dict is built before the agent runs, so escalation_share_test, n_work_orders_*, audit_records, severity counts and elapsed_s are never logged to MLflow.
findings.evidence: artifacts/mlflow.db latest_metrics for run a9e6712863f2 (FD001 full) contains hgbr_rmse_capped, picp_test_capped, mpiw_test, agent_max_width ... but no escalation_share_test, elapsed_s or n_work_orders_batch; viewdata.py:71 column list; dashboard.py:47 `st.sidebar.markdown(f"**Model version** `{m.get('mlflow_run_id', 'local')}` ...")`.
